stories.headline: NFL playoff chance tiers: Where all 32 teams fit in 2026 postseason picture
stories.summary: We placed all 32 NFL teams into tiers based on their likelihood of making the playoffs, from Super Bowl favorites to the top draft pick candidates.
stories.body:
The back half of the 2026 NFL season is upon us, and the playoff race is heating up. Though the standings tell us a lot about teams' chances to reach the postseason, they don't tell us everything. Team strength, injuries, tiebreakers, future strength of schedule and more can shift those odds up or down and don't show up in the win or loss columns.

So, ESPN analytics writer Seth Walder placed all 32 teams into eight tiers of playoff hopes, ranging from clear Super Bowl contenders to those already looking ahead to 2027. There is some fluidity in between, because for as confident as we feel about the league right now, things could look quite different once Week 18 rolls around. The tiers are based on information from ESPN's Football Power Index (FPI), betting lines, metrics, health status and some instinct.

Walder ranked the teams within each tier too. All percentages and statistical rankings are through the Sunday late afternoon window unless otherwise indicated, and playoff chances are from the FPI.

Jump to a team:

ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN

CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND

JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN

NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF

SEA | TB | TEN | WSH

Tier 1: True Super Bowl contenders

San Francisco 49ers (8-1)
Chances to make the playoffs: 99.8%

Chances to win the NFC West: 96.2%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 39.8%

Injuries have hit some of the 49ers' best players -- edge rusher Nick Bosa missed five games and wide receiver Mike Evans hasn't played since Week 6 -- but San Francisco is the FPI's Super Bowl favorite for two main reasons. The Niners are basically a lock to reach the playoffs and a heavy favorite to win the NFC West given their current lead and head-to-head wins over the Rams and the Seahawks. Brock Purdy entered Week 10 as the No. 1 quarterback in QBR, and he is arguably the league's MVP thus far. Kyle Shanahan might be the Coach of the Year thus far too.

See remaining schedule

Buffalo Bills (8-1)
Chances to make the playoffs: >99.9%

Chances to win the AFC East: 99.7%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 31.0%

The Bills entered this season as the AFC favorite, and nothing that has happened in the first 10 weeks has dispelled that notion. Their hold on the conference looks even stronger now than it did then thanks to their conference-best record and the Ravens falling out of contention. Buffalo's defense (16th in EPA per play) is still a concern, but quarterback Josh Allen, running back James Cook III and the Bills' offensive line do more than enough damage on offense.

See remaining schedule

Jacksonville Jaguars (7-2)
Chances to make the playoffs: 99.9%

Chances to win the AFC South: 98.8%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 22.9%

The Jaguars were already playoff locks and clearly one of the top two teams in the AFC before the trade deadline, when they acquired safety Jessie Bates III along with defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux. The Davis deal from the Jaguars' perspective is one of the worst trades in years, but there's also little doubt Jacksonville is better today than it was a week ago. And the Jaguars were great a week ago! The Jaguars rank in the top five in EPA per dropback on offense and EPA allowed per dropback as well as EPA allowed per designed rush on defense.

See remaining schedule

Tier 2: Playoff locks

Kansas City Chiefs (7-2)
Chances to make the playoffs: 99.3%

Chances to win the AFC West: 45.8%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 18.2%

The Chiefs faced three major questions entering the season:

How would quarterback Patrick Mahomes fare after recovering from a torn ACL suffered last December?
What kind of impact would free agent running back Kenneth Walker III have on the offense?
Could the defense survive the loss of starting cornerbacks Trent McDuffie and Jaylen Watson?

The answer to every question has been positive for Kansas City. In particular, Walker has helped transform the Chiefs' rushing attack into a strength. And coordinator Steve Spagnuolo has managed to keep the defense strong too: It ranks sixth in EPA per play.

See remaining schedule

Cincinnati Bengals (6-2)
Chances to make the playoffs: 99%

Chances to win the AFC North: 77.4%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 14%

It's something we've wondered about for years: What would happen if the Bengals could manager to combine a peak Joe Burrow season with simply mediocre defense? Well, we're finding out. Burrow is in the MVP race, and Cincinnati's defense is ranked 11th in EPA per play. Wide receivers Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins have been outstanding and provide a sky-high ceiling for the passing offense. Plus, the Bengals have a very easy schedule the rest of the way.

See remaining schedule

Denver Broncos (7-2)
Chances to make the playoffs: 99.3%

Chances to win the AFC West: 54.2%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 9.2%

Somehow, it's working. Despite Bo Nix falling well short of expectations -- he entered Week 10 ranked 24th out of 31 qualifiers in QBR -- the Broncos are a virtual lock to reach the playoffs and have a great shot at winning the AFC West. The defense hasn't quite lived up to its reputation (13th in EPA per play), but Denver also hasn't had All-Pro cornerback Pat Surtain II for every game, either. If the offense can keep its recent momentum (the Broncos have put up 26 points in each of their past three games), Denver can be a threat in the postseason. The Broncos have a soft schedule the rest of the way too.

See remaining schedule

Tier 3: Likely in, barring a collapse

Minnesota Vikings (7-2)
Chances to make the playoffs: 95.5%

Chances to win the NFC North: 42.0%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 13.1%

Minnesota's trade-deadline deal for quarterback Kirk Cousins breathed new life into its season. That move instantly increased the Vikings' playoff chances from 65% to 83% at the time of the deal, according to the FPI. But that deal was about what comes next. With Brian Flores' incredible defense leading the way, the Vikings can and should have legitimate Super Bowl aspirations. The moment Flores leaves, a real possibility in this upcoming offseason, the team's contention window vanishes, so the Vikings need to take advantage of this opportunity. Minnesota's 30-10 dismantling of the Packers on Sunday only reinforced what a good trade it was.

See remaining schedule

Chicago Bears (7-2)
Chances to make the playoffs: 85.9%

Chances to win the NFC North: 21.7%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 12.1%

Chicago entered its bye week as a near lock to reach the playoffs and very much a team that could go all the way. Quarterback Caleb Williams has taken a significant step forward, and the fact that the Bears are 7-2 despite Williams missing three games is a testament to the coaching staff and how strong this team is. Coordinator Dennis Allen was already getting the most out of a lacking defensive roster when the Bears acquired the best defensive tackle in the league in Jeffery Simmons as they prepare for what they hope is a Super Bowl run.

See remaining schedule

Detroit Lions (7-2)
Chances to make the playoffs: 89.8%

Chances to win the NFC North: 35.2%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 10.2%

If they played in a normal division, the Lions would be even safer than this, especially after the team's blowout win over the Patriots in Munich on Sunday -- albeit with New England missing quarterback Drake Maye for most of that contest. But Detroit's record has it on the verge of a playoff berth despite playing in a stacked NFC North and with the Seahawks and Rams looming as other wild-card threats. There's little doubt the Lions can score points. But the X factor down the stretch and in the postseason will be their defense, which ranks 23rd in EPA per play and now faces the possibility of a significant knee injury to star edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson.

See remaining schedule

Pittsburgh Steelers (6-2)
Chances to make the playoffs: 87.3%

Chances to win the AFC North: 19.9%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 2.6%

The Steelers are barreling toward another playoff berth thanks to their running game and defense. No team in the league is more efficient (by EPA per play) on the ground than the Steelers -- hello, Jaylen Warren! -- and the team's run defense hasn't allowed opponents to rush successfully against them. Getting past the Bengals to win the division will be a tall order, but the fall of the Ravens helps widen the Steelers' path to the postseason.

See remaining schedule

Tier 4: We're leaning yes

Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6)
Chances to make the playoffs: 61.1%

Chances to win the NFC South: 60.9%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 5.0%

The FPI believes the Bucs are the best team in the NFC South by a wide margin. That's a low bar to clear, but finishing atop the division is all that matters for Tampa Bay to reach the playoffs -- as it's the only way it will get there. Quarterback Baker Mayfield missed three games (and didn't complete a pass in a bizarre win Nov. 1 over the Falcons in a monsoon), but he has played poorly when on the field. Mayfield entered Week 10 ahead of only Justin Herbert in QBR. And now Mayfield's status is in doubt for Week 11 due to an injury suffered last week. Still, thanks to Todd Bowles' defense -- and a reasonable belief that the passing offense will be better going forward -- the Bucs are the NFC South favorites.

See remaining schedule

Seattle Seahawks (6-4)
Chances to make the playoffs: 48.8%

Chances to win the NFC West: 2.3%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 5.6%

This isn't how the Seahawks envisioned their title defense going. The defense has lived up to its end of the bargain, ranking fourth in EPA per play entering Sunday. But Sam Darnold has not. Darnold ranked 23rd in QBR entering Sunday, registering only 6.8 air yards per attempt (27th highest out of 31 qualifiers) and a 3.8% interception rate (30th). A quad injury knocked Darnold out of the lineup in Weeks 9 and 10, but the Seahawks managed to win both games. With all four teams in the NFC North in the playoff picture along with three NFC West teams (49ers, Seahawks and Rams), there will be a fight for the wild cards. After their win Sunday, the Seahawks are essentially a coin flip to make the playoffs.

See remaining schedule

Tier 5: On the fringe of hope and despair

Los Angeles Rams (6-4)
Chances to make the playoffs: 46.0%

Chances to win the NFC West: 1.5%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 7.6%

If the Rams can reach the playoffs and get wide receivers Puka Nacua and Davante Adams back, they will absolutely be a Super Bowl contender. But that's a big if at this stage. Los Angeles' offense never looked as prolific as we imagined it would in the offseason -- ranking only eighth in EPA per play -- and it will now have to navigate at least a few more weeks without either of its top two receivers. The good news is that edge rusher Myles Garrett (who missed seven games) and cornerback Trent McDuffie (missed three) are back on the field, though CB Jaylen Watson is lost for the season.

See remaining schedule

Cleveland Browns (6-4)
Chances to make the playoffs: 49.0%

Chances to win the AFC North: 2.6%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: Seemingly against all odds, the Browns are still in the playoff mix. The team's young core has been impressive and playing well, with the 2026 draft class contributing right away and following in the footsteps of the exceptional 2025 crop. Two factors are holding Cleveland back: the offensive line and quarterback Deshaun Watson. Despite the narrative about his improved play, Watson ranked 28th in QBR entering Sunday. Still, after the Browns came back to beat the Texans on Sunday (their sixth come-from-behind win of the campaign), the Browns' playoff chances took a big jump. They have a real shot.

See remaining schedule

New York Giants (5-3-1)
Chances to make the playoffs: 44.7%

Chances to win the NFC East: 44.5%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 0.7%

There's a shocking amount of optimism for the Giants during a season in which they lost starting quarterback Jaxson Dart to injury. J.J. McCarthy (acquired via trade) has looked better than expected, rookie linebacker Arvell Reese seems like a big hit and somehow the Giants are in first place in the lowly NFC East. But can McCarthy (who has only a 53.9 QBR this season) really be trusted? We'll find out in the back half of the campaign. And after New York's loss to the Commanders on Thursday, the Giants' playoff position is looking shakier than it was entering Week 10.

See remaining schedule

Dallas Cowboys (4-6)
Chances to make the playoffs: 41.6%

Chances to win the NFC East: 41.4%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 2.5%

The NFC East has been there for the taking, but the Cowboys haven't managed to seize control. The FPI believes Dallas is the best team in the division, but the Cowboys have stumbled throughout the first half of the season, with the defense -- which entered Sunday ranking 30th in EPA per play -- holding the team back, per usual. That was never more evident than in Sunday's 46-40 loss to the 49ers. Washington's win over the Giants on Thursday helped Dallas, because essentially the only way the Cowboys can reach the playoffs is by winning the NFC East.

See remaining schedule

New England Patriots (5-5)
Chances to make the playoffs: 36.5%

Chances to win the AFC East: 0.3%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 0.9%

The Patriots' playoff chances potentially took a big hit at the end of their first drive Sunday, when Drake Maye was knocked out of the game with an ankle injury. The Patriots went on to lose 35-10 to fall to .500. Suddenly, the Patriots, who had a good chance at reaching the playoffs before Sunday, are on the rocks -- and Maye's health will be a huge factor in where their season will ultimately end up. The Patriots' 1-2 start -- and Maye's 51.1 QBR in those first three games -- could loom large and reduces the margin for error even more.

See remaining schedule

Green Bay Packers (6-4)
Chances to make the playoffs: 33.1%

Chances to win the NFC North: 1.1%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 2.2%

There have been moments when quarterback Jordan Love has looked like an MVP candidate and the Packers seem like one of the best teams in football. But because of their offensive line-fueled 1-2 start, their 30-10 home loss to the Vikings on Sunday and their placement in a division with four good teams, Green Bay is suddenly on shaky playoff ground. Like many NFC wild-card hopefuls, the Packers would be real contenders -- with Love throwing to receivers Christian Watson and Matthew Golden -- if they can get into the postseason. But there is work to do to get there.

See remaining schedule

Carolina Panthers (4-5)
Chances to make the playoffs: 31.6%

Chances to win the NFC South: 31.2%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 0.8%

A hot start from Bryce Young (ranked seventh in QBR through Week 5) had the Panthers at 3-2. But he hasn't kept up that pace, and the defense has been below average. The result? A three-game losing streak that dropped Carolina back into the messy mix that is the NFC South. But they could still win the woebegone division, especially after beating the Saints at the buzzer on Sunday to end that losing skid. So Carolina is atop the division right now, though the FPI still believes the Buccaneers are the favorite.

See remaining schedule

Tier 6: Stranger things have happened

Houston Texans (3-6)
Chances to make the playoffs: 21.9%

Chances to win the AFC South: 1.1%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 1.0%

An 0-4 start put Houston in a dire situation, but the Texans clawed themselves back into the playoff race with a 3-1 stretch. But they threw away many of those gains with an upset loss to the Browns on Sunday that set Houston way back. C.J. Stroud has played well (he was sixth in QBR entering Sunday), but the Texans' defense has been surprisingly mediocre. Such is the variant nature of that side of the ball sometimes -- even when a team has young stars like the Texans do.

See remaining schedule

Washington Commanders (3-5-1)
Chances to make the playoffs: 14.0%

Chances to win the NFC East: 13.9%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: 0.3%

The Commanders gave themselves hope with their victory in a back-and-forth game against the Giants on Thursday night. Not only do they now have three wins (and a tie). but also the head-to-head tiebreaker over New York. Quarterback Jayden Daniels has played fairly well when active (12th best QBR entering Sunday), so if the Commanders can keep him upright they have a long-shot chance.

See remaining schedule

Baltimore Ravens (4-5)
Chances to make the playoffs: 5.0%

Chances to win the AFC North: Chances to make the Super Bowl: Can the Jacoby Brissett-led Ravens win enough games to keep the team in contention and buy time until Lamar Jackson is able to return from injury? Basically, everything hinges on that and Jackson's return timeline. If the Ravens can somehow reach the playoffs with a healthy Jackson, they would be Super Bowl contenders. But that is a tall, tall order.

See remaining schedule

Tier 7: Yes, I'm telling you there's a (slight) chance

New Orleans Saints (3-6)
Chances to make the playoffs: 6.1%

Chances to win the NFC South: 6.0%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: Just like the other NFC South teams, the Saints' season hasn't gone great. New Orleans has had its moments -- like the surprising Week 2 win over Lamar Jackson and the Ravens -- but ultimately has had more downs than ups. Still, the Saints remain in the sub-.500-mix for the division crown, though they're a long shot now after Sunday's loss to the Panthers.

See remaining schedule

Atlanta Falcons (3-7)
Chances to make the playoffs: 1.8%

Chances to win the NFC South: 1.8%

Chances to make the Super Bowl: Atlanta signaled what it thought of its season at the trade deadline, when it dealt away star safety Jessie Bates III and starting center Ryan Neuzil. Trading away Bates made sense given that the Falcons aren't really contenders (they're just lucky enough to play in the NFC South) and were unlikely to get a compensatory pick for him if he left. But still, it accentuated that the Falcons don't have real expectations about 2026. The FPI agrees, giving Atlanta the lowest odds to win the NFC South.

See remaining schedule

Las Vegas Raiders (4-6)
Chances to make the playoffs: 1.4%

Chances to win the AFC West: Chances to make the Super Bowl: The Raiders got out to a hot 3-0 start before dropping four straight. Even though they were 4-5 at the trade deadline, they (rightfully!) decided to deal quarterback Kirk Cousins for a third-round pick, prompting the start of the Fernando Mendoza era in Week 10. No matter who was at quarterback, reaching the playoffs would have been something of a dream for Las Vegas at this point. I'm leaving the door the slightest bit ajar, though, in case Mendoza can take the league by storm from this point forward.

See remaining schedule

Indianapolis Colts (3-7)
Chances to make the playoffs: 1.4%

Chances to win the AFC South: Chances to make the Super Bowl: Even though quarterback Daniel Jones was able to play at the start of the season, the Colts were never able to re-find the magic they possessed at the start of the 2025 campaign. Instead, they fired GM Chris Ballard and kicked off a fire sale, dealing away many of their good players (but not Jonathan Taylor for some reason). This team has no shot in 2026 and, to make it sting even worse, the Jets own their 2027 first-round pick.

See remaining schedule

Tier 8: Just rest up for 2027

Philadelphia Eagles (2-7)
Chances to make the playoffs: 0.2%

Fret not, Eagles fans, because if there's one thing Philadelphia does better than any other team in the league, it's taking advantage of the opportunity a losing season provides. Recognizing that they had virtually no shot at the playoffs with quarterback Jalen Hurts out for the season, the Eagles made some amazing pre-deadline trades, somehow getting a second-round pick (plus a day-3 pick swap!) for center Cam Jurgens and first- and second-round picks for Jordan Davis. So sure, 2026 is effectively over for the Eagles, but they set themselves up so well for 2027 and beyond.

See remaining schedule

New York Jets (2-8)
Chances to make the playoffs: On the surface it's been a rough season, but in some ways it's actually been perfect for New York's long-term growth. The Jets' core young players -- edge rusher David Bailey, wide receivers Omar Cooper Jr. and Adonai Mitchell and tight end Kenyon Sadiq -- have all played well, or at least flashed their abilities. But the Jets have still lost games, which helps their draft stock for next year (which includes three first-round picks). Sure, this season is over. But give this team a new quarterback and a new head coach and it can get good, fast. I am uncomfortably bullish on the Jets for 2027 and beyond.

See remaining schedule

Arizona Cardinals (3-7)
Chances to make the playoffs: Any optimism around Arizona after its shocking Week 1 win over the Chargers (which is less shocking given what we know about Los Angeles now) was short-lived. Fast-forward to now. and the Cardinals have traded their first bridge quarterback, Jacoby Brissett, while their second bridge quarterback (Gardner Minshew II) is now on injured reserve. So, they have turned to rookie Carson Beck, which is where this season was always destined, and looking ahead to 2027.

See remaining schedule

Los Angeles Chargers (0-8)
Chances to make the playoffs: This has been a pure, unmitigated disaster. Like so many others, I fell for the Chargers in the offseason. I thought they were legitimate contenders with Mike McDaniel running the offense and offensive tackles Joe Alt and Rashawn Slater back from injury. How wrong I was. I'm still confused to how things got to this point. Justin Herbert entered Sunday ranked last in QBR, and the Chargers' season has been over for weeks.

See remaining schedule

Tennessee Titans (1-8)
Chances to make the playoffs: After Sunday, the Titans rank 26th in offensive EPA per play and 29th in defensive EPA per play. That's not a recipe for success, and there has been very little of it in Tennessee this season. Cam Ward has played better this season (21st in QBR entering Sunday) than last, but how he plays down the stretch and how the upcoming draft shakes out will determine his role in 2027 and beyond.

See remaining schedule

Miami Dolphins (1-8)
Chances to make the playoffs: The Dolphins have shown fight, but ultimately this team's lackluster roster wasn't quite frisky enough to pick off a few games. The Malik Willis experiment at quarterback went OK. I personally had lofty expectations for Willis heading into this season that he did not meet, but it hasn't been awful, either. He ranked 20th in QBR heading into Sunday and now is on injured reserve with a groin injury. His status beyond this season likely hinges on how Miami approaches the 2027 NFL draft.

See remaining schedule

stories.headline: 2027 WNBA mock draft: Tempo win lottery, projected to pick JuJu Watkins at No. 1
stories.summary: Toronto edged Houston and got the top pick in Sunday's draft lottery. The Comets will pick No. 2 and the Mystics No. 3.
stories.body:
In what could be the JuJu Watkins sweepstakes, the Toronto Tempo will have the No. 1 pick in the 2027 WNBA draft. The Tempo won the draft lottery Sunday, with the Houston Comets picking second and the Washington Mystics third.

The Seattle Storm have the No. 4 pick, the Portland Fire got No. 5 and the Los Angeles Sparks have Nos. 6 and 7.

The Tempo, an expansion team in 2026, finished 11-33 last season, missing the playoffs. They were last in the league in defensive rating and won just one game after the All-Star break.

All of that could be much improved in 2027 with a player such as Watkins in Toronto. The national player of the year as a sophomore for the USC Trojans, Watkins missed last season after a knee injury suffered in the 2025 NCAA tournament. She has looked great so far this season and would fit in well with any WNBA team.

This is just Watkins' third college season, but age-wise, she is eligible for the draft. It is unknown if she will go pro or return to USC, but for now we are including her in the mock draft. If she decides Toronto is an unappealing destination or just wants to spend another season in college, she can wait until the 2028 draft.

That said, there is also uncertainty about the seniors who already have completed three seasons. Under the NCAA's new age-based eligibility model -- the five-seasons-in-five-years rule -- they could return for the 2027-28 season. So a lot about the draft pool remains speculative.

But now we know the lottery order.

1. Toronto Tempo: JuJu Watkins
USC | guard | 6-foot-2 | senior

Watkins and the Trojans are 3-1 after a close loss Sunday to No. 1 South Carolina in which she had 25 points. The March 2025 knee injury that forced Watkins to miss last season has not slowed her. She is averaging 24.5 points, 6.8 rebounds, 3.5 assists and 3.3 steals. The Tempo's strength last season was at guard, led by Marina Mabrey. If Watkins doesn't declare for the draft, there should still be good players available for the Tempo. But perhaps not an immediate franchise-changer as Watkins is expected to be.

2. Houston Comets: Madison Booker
Texas | forward | 6-foot-1 | senior

Like several teams, Texas has not been tested yet. But Booker has displayed why she's a lottery pick in the three games she has played so far, including a 30-point, six-assist game against Northern Colorado. Booker's size, strength and confidence on offense and her versatility on defense should translate to the pro game. She took a hard fall in Wednesday's win over South Dakota State and did not play in Sunday's victory against Tarleton State, but she is not expected to miss much more time. The Comets -- the Connecticut Sun relocated as a revived franchise -- last played in the 2008 WNBA season. The Sun were tied for next to last with Toronto at 11-33 this year, and it's fair to say they could use help in all areas, which would make Booker appealing.

3. Washington Mystics: Hannah Hidalgo
Notre Dame | guard | 5-foot-6 | senior

Hidalgo has carried a heavy load throughout her college career, and that continues her senior season. In four victories, she has averaged 28.3 points, 7.5 rebounds, 5.5 assists and 4.8 steals while shooting 59.4% from the field. Hidalgo is a huge threat on offense and defense and could really add to the young core already there if she goes to the Mystics. Washington could use more 3-point shooting. While Hidalgo wasn't great from beyond the arc last season (36-of-142, 25.4%), she shot 40% from 3-point range as a sophomore and is at 40% so far this season.

4. Seattle Storm: Tessa Johnson
South Carolina | guard | 6-foot-1 | senior

Johnson's 3-point shooting is an impressive tool that will translate to the pro game. She was the top power conference player in the country last season in 3-point percentage (44.8%, 90 of 201). So far this season, she has made 9 of 18 (50%) from behind the arc and is averaging 17.0 points. She had 28 points in Sunday's victory over USC. The Storm were last in the WNBA this past season at 8-36 and could benefit from another dynamic young guard to go along with the young post talent they have.

5. Portland Fire: Mikaylah Williams
LSU | guard | 6-foot | senior

The Tigers have cruised through four blowouts and Williams' averages -- 19.0 points, 5.3 rebounds and 5.5 assists while shooting 58% from the field and 45.5% from behind the arc -- don't tell us anything we didn't expect. She's a pro-ready player on the offensive end who can look to improve defensively in the WNBA. The expansion Fire had a solid season in 2025, going 17-27, and Williams could fit in offensively.

6. Los Angeles Sparks: Kymora Johnson
Virginia | guard | 5-foot-7 | senior

The Cavaliers are 5-0, and we will know more about them a team once they play their tougher nonconference foes, such as Oklahoma on Nov. 23. But so far, Johnson has looked very good, averaging 18.8 points, 5.2 rebounds, 5.4 assists and 2.2 steals while shooting 59.6% from the field and 61.3% from behind the arc (13 of 21). With back-to-back picks, Los Angeles can address two of several needs with this draft. The Sparks were 16-28 this season and missed the playoffs for the sixth year in a row.

7. Los Angeles Sparks: Sarah Cissé
France | forward | 6-foot-2

There's so much we don't know now about the Sparks -- including who their coach will be for 2027 - as they move on after future Hall of Famer Nneka Ogwumike's retirement. But Cissé is another talented player out of France who could make an impact on the WNBA. The MVP of the U20 European Championships this summer, she turns 20 in January. The Sparks were next-to-last in the WNBA in rebounding this past season, so Cissé might be able to help there.

8. New York Liberty: Ainhoa Risacher
France | forward | 6-foot-1

If you recognize the last name, Risacher is the younger sister of Zaccharie Risacher, the NBA's No. 1 draft pick in 2024. A good-sized wing player, Risacher competed alongside Cissé on France's winning U20 European Championships team this past summer. She will turn 20 in July. The Liberty had an up-and-down 2026 season, getting the No. 8 seed in the playoffs. They knocked off No. 1 Minnesota, but then were swept by No. 4 Atlanta. New York fired Chris DeMarco after just one season, so we await their next coach. The Liberty already have a strong French/international presence. The question might be if Risacher impresses them enough defensively compared to other draft options.

9. Dallas Wings: Chloe Kitts
South Carolina | forward | 6-foot-2 | senior

Kitts missed last season because of a knee injury but has looked great so far. A starter as a junior, she averaged 10.2 points and 7.7 rebounds in 2024-25. Through four games this season, she has three double-doubles and is averaging 13.0 points and 10.0 rebounds. In Sunday's victory over USC, Kitts had 15 points, 12 rebounds, three assists and four steals. If she continues to play this well, we could see her move up the draft board. Still, with Dallas having young guards such as Paige Bueckers and Azzi Fudd, Kitts could be a good addition for the Wings, who made the playoffs at 27-17 this season.

10. Indiana Fever: Talaysia Cooper
Ole Miss | guard | 6-foot-0 | senior

The Fever are facing two huge offseason questions: Will free-agent guard Kelsey Mitchell return, and who will be their general manager? Indiana could use help at the wing position with a player who can defend at a high level but also score. That could be Cooper, who is playing for her third SEC program and averaging 14.0 points while shooting 37% (10 of 27) from 3-point range. She showed progress from behind the arc last season, and if that continues this season it will help her draft prospects. Cooper had her best defensive season as a sophomore at Tennessee, and a return to that level will boost her.

11. Chicago Sky: Khamil Pierre
NC State | forward | 6-foot-2 | senior

Pierre doesn't shoot the 3 much, but she is relentless in the paint. After two strong years at Vanderbilt, she transferred to NC State and led the ACC in rebounding last season (11.9 RPG) while averaging 16.7 points and shooting 52.5% from the field. So far this season for the 4-1 Wolfpack, she is averaging 21.2 points and 8.4 rebounds while shooting 51.3%. The injury-plagued Sky went 16-28 and missed the playoffs for the third year in a row this past season. They were 13th in offensive rating and 10th in rebounding, and Pierre might help both areas.

12. Chicago Sky: S'Mya Nichols
Kansas | guard | 6-foot | senior

Nichols is off to a little slower start than expected, averaging 12.5 points and 4.3 assists (she averaged 17.4 and 4.6 last season). That's why she has fallen from No. 6 in our two previous mock drafts. But to be fair, it's still early in the season. Nichols had 12 points and six assists in the Jayhawks' loss to Nebraska on Saturday. She and Kansas have another shot at a ranked team this week at Minnesota on Wednesday.

13. Dallas Wings: Kaylene Smikle
Tennessee | guard | 6-foot-0 | senior

Smikle started her career at Rutgers, then went to Maryland and is now at Tennessee. She played just seven games last year with the Terps, but then missed the rest of the season after knee surgery. So far this season, she is leading the 4-0 Lady Vols with 22.3 points per game, while also averaging 6.0 rebounds. She is also off to a hot start from behind the arc at 50% (12 of 24). Smikle could add guard/wing depth for Dallas.

14. Golden State Valkyries: Oluchi Okananwa
Maryland | guard | 5-foot-10 | senior

Okananwa is averaging 14.0 points and 6.3 rebounds, but the Terps have played just three games. She was first team all-Big Ten and all-defense last season -- we know the WNBA champion Valkyries love defense -- but she probably will need to show improvement as a 3-point shooter to ensure being a first-round pick. So far this season, she has made 3-for-6 from behind the arc.

15. Minnesota Lynx: Clara Strack
Kentucky | center | 6-foot-5 | senior

Sunday was another big stats day for Strack, who had 29 points and 18 rebounds in a victory over Eastern Michigan. That included going 4-of-5 from behind the arc, which is important: It's not easy for traditional centers to find their way in the WNBA, so having shooting range matters. Strack has shown that, making 42 3-pointers over the last two seasons. She is 8-of-21 from 3-point range so far this season. Strack, who was the SEC's defensive player of the year in 2025, is averaging 18.4 points, 9.6 rebounds and 3.8 blocks for the 5-0 Wildcats.

stories.headline: Which NHL coaches have the most wins in history?
stories.summary: Scotty Bowman leads all NHL coaches in wins all-time. Find out who else makes the list.
stories.body:
From Paul Maurice and Joel Quenneville to Lindy Ruff and John Tortorella, the NHL has its fair share of all-time great coaches. But all of them are chasing the accomplishments of Scotty Bowman.

The Montreal native won a record nine Stanley Cups in 30 seasons behind the bench, five with the Montreal Canadiens, three with the Detroit Red Wings and one with the Pittsburgh Penguins. Bowman twice won the Jack Adams Award, the honor presented annually to the NHL's top coach.

stories.headline: Spain 'overwhelmed' by 'exceptional' England: We also know how to lose
stories.summary: Coach Luis de la Fuente said Spain were "overwhelmed" in the early stages of Sunday's 3-2 UEFA Nations League defeat to England, but backed his team to return stronger after seeing their three-year unbeaten run come to an end.
stories.body:
Coach Luis de la Fuente said Spain were "overwhelmed" in the early stages of Sunday's 3-2 UEFA Nations League defeat to England, but backed his team to return stronger after seeing their three-year unbeaten run come to an end.

Spain trailed 3-0 at the Metropolitano before goals from Mikel Oyarzabal and Nico Williams --- both created by Lamine Yamal -- saw them come close to pulling off a dramatic comeback.

The reigning world and European champions hadn't lost a competitive game in 43 matches, but now finish second behind England in their Nations League group, meaning a tougher draw for next year's quarterfinals.

"I take away only positives [from the game]," De la Fuente said in his postmatch news conference. "It highlights just how difficult it is to reach the level we've reached.

"Just as we know how to win, we also know how to lose. It's true that we were overwhelmed in the first 30 minutes, but I really believed we would mount a comeback in the final stages."

Spain had beaten England 3-2 at Wembley in their previous meeting in September. They will find out who they'll face in the next round of the Nations League in Friday's draw in Nyon, Switzerland.

"It's a shame we have to wait until March [to play again]," De la Fuente said on Sunday. "We'll like to have another game next week. But we'll head into that knockout tie with a real desire to win."

De la Fuente refused to be critical of his team, who were second-best to an exceptional England for the first 60 minutes.

"We faced an exceptional national team today," De la Fuente said. "It only underscores the value of everything we've achieved so far.

"I'm already looking forward to the next training camp. The team is motivated to take on a new challenge."

stories.headline: Andy Burnham urges caution on potential moves to scrap Premier League 3pm blackout
stories.summary: Prime Minister Andy Burnham says he would "urge caution" on scrapping the Saturday 3pm blackout.
stories.body:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham says he would "urge caution" on scrapping the Saturday 3pm blackout, and called for broadcasters to be mindful of the impact on fans caused by changes to kick-off times.

The ban on broadcasting live matches between 2.45 p.m. and 5.15 p.m on Saturdays was introduced in the 1960s but it could be dropped for the next set of Premier League, EFL and Scottish Professional Football League (SPFL) rights cycles from 2029-30.

The purpose of the blackout has been to protect live attendance at matches, amid fears crowds would be affected, especially in lower league or non-league football, if top-flight matches were available to watch on television or streaming services.

Burnham said any decision to remove the ban would require careful thought about the consequences.

"I would urge a bit of caution on it [the blackout], because it does protect the income of lower league clubs," he said.

"If you have effectively wall-to-wall Premier League football at any time, it takes away perhaps the incentive to go and watch the football league or non-league.

"So I think it has to be considered carefully. I'm not going to take the pure consumer view here. I'll take the health of football approach to this particular issue.

"I would first of all want to protect the football pyramid before I agree to saying 'let's have even more live football."

- Andy Burnham to publish Man City mayoral dealings after intervention draws criticism

- UK PM Burnham wants 'outdated' football drinking ban scrapped

"I think it's about protecting the experience with the paying supporter, protecting the football pyramid. Those issues matter to me, first of all."

The trend in television rights has been to offer more matches in order to keep revenues up -- the current Premier League deal includes 270 live matches compared to 200 in the previous one for example.

The logical conclusion of that trend is for all matches to be made available live, and the SPFL's tender for its next set of rights is reported to offer the chance to do just that.

The blackout is enforced by article 48 of UEFA's statutes, which the Football Association and the Scottish Football Association choose to impose.

It applies when 50% or more of matches in the top two divisions are due to be played simultaneously.

Premier League chief executive Richard Masters told talkSPORT in August that English football was leaning towards a blackout but added: "It's not just us involved in the decision about article 48. It's us, the EFL and the FA.

""We've got to take that decision at some point in the future about whether things are going to change.

"It's not a decision for now. It's a decision we've got to make before the next set of domestic processes that the EFL and the Premier League are going to do.

"I'd say in about 18 months time we'll come back to that decision about whether article 48 should remain or not."

Burnham was also asked if broadcasters needed to be more mindful of the disruption caused to fans by the scheduling of matches for live broadcast.

"It doesn't give any regard, actually, as far as I can see, to travelling supporters," he said.

"Monday night games, you know, people in the north-east coming to the north-west, it's not fair, the way that is done, or very early kick-offs on Saturday, very difficult for people to get there. So on that, I agree [with the need to be more mindful].

stories.headline: Tim Hill, Yankees agree to 1-year, $2.25M deal, sources say
stories.summary: Left-hander Tim Hill is staying with the Yankees, agreeing to a one-year, $2.25 million contract, sources told ESPN.
stories.body:
Left-hander Tim Hill is staying with the New York Yankees, agreeing to a one-year, $2.25 million contract, sources told ESPN's Jeff Passan on Sunday.

Hill's deal includes a $2.5 million club option for 2028, sources said.

A 36-year-old reliever, Hill was 5-2 with a 4.60 ERA and two saves in 58⅔ innings over 67 appearances last season. He allowed a career-high 12 homers, three more than his previous high.

Hill's 68.8% ground ball percentage led the major leagues among pitchers with 50 or more innings. He held left-handed batters to a .213 batting average while righties hit .293 against him.

New York signed Hill in June 2024 following his release by the Chicago White Sox. He is a nine-year major league veteran who also has pitched for Kansas City (2018-19) and San Diego (2020-23).

He had a $3 million salary this year under an option the Yankees exercised then became a free agent.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Ciryl Gane survives early onslaught, edges Josh Hokit in UFC 334 main event
stories.summary: Ciryl Gane got all he could handle from Josh Hokit in a five-round slugfest but took command late to defend his heavyweight title at UFC 334.
stories.body:
NEW YORK -- In the end, Josh Hokit proved to be more than just a shtick.

Ciryl Gane defended his UFC heavyweight championship Saturday by outlasting Hokit in a spirited five-round main event at UFC 334 at Madison Square Garden. All three judges scored the bout 48-47 for Gane in his second title defense; he previously scored a second-round stoppage over Alex Pereira in June at the White House.

Despite Gane (15-2) getting the decision, Hokit (10-1) might have won the night. Hokit, 29, was a relative unknown when he joined the UFC just 15 months ago, but he has quickly built his name around controversial -- at times, ugly -- trash talk.

On Saturday, however, he showed that there is plenty of substance behind the persona. He pushed Gane backward with relentless pressure and won over the New York crowd with his durability and willingness to press forward.

"I will rejoice in my suffering," Hokit said in his postfight Octagon interview. "Suffering builds endurance. Endurance builds character. Character builds hope. I will never lose hope. I will be champion one day. You guys can kick me when I'm down, I'll still break your f---ing leg."

Gane, whose only losses have come against Jon Jones and Francis Ngannou, credited Hokit's approach and said he expected a challenge Saturday despite oddsmakers listing him as a clear favorite.

"All the people around the world [took him lightly], but not me," Gane said. "This guy is a motherf---er. He did very well."

According to UFC Stats, Gane outlanded Hokit 298-243 in total strikes, and their 541 combined strikes set a record for a heavyweight bout. Gane's 237 significant strikes also broke the UFC heavyweight record.

Much of that volume could be attributed to Hokit's game plan. He ran at Gane from the opening bell and set a frantic pace of striking and grappling exchanges. Gane did well to disrupt his pressure with jabs and body punches, but Hokit weathered the shots well. He electrified the New York crowd with a huge slam at the end of the first round and appeared to hold momentum through the second and third rounds.

"There's no doubt that Hokit's stock goes up, even with me," UFC CEO Dana White said. "I thought this guy was a bigmouthed goofball, and I hated his shtick and the whole thing. I respect the s--- out of that guy. He is the real deal."

Gane's championship background showed in the final two rounds. He continued to land knees and punches to the body and took control of the striking exchanges in the final round.

The win could set up potential rematches for Gane against Pereira, former champion Tom Aspinall and Alexander Volkov, as well as a new matchup against Russian knockout artist Sergei Pavlovich.

stories.body:
Formula 1 is back under the bright lights of Las Vegas for one of the most extravagant weekends on the calendar.

Lando Norris clinched his third victory this season at the São Paulo Grand Prix after new world champion Kimi Antonelli spun out of the lead in wet conditions.

Max Verstappen had a masterful drive in his Red Bull and charged his way through the field from 21st to second.

So you don't miss a thing, here's everything you need to know for the 21st round.

How to watch

Every practice and qualifying session as well as the race itself will be available to watch on Sky Sports F1. The sessions are also on Sky Sports Main Event.

For non-subscribers, highlights of the Las Vegas Grand Prix will be on free-to-air television on Channel 4.

In the U.S., subscribers can watch every session on Apple TV, via a new F1 channel on the platform.

Las Vegas Strip Circuit
Las Vegas' race is certainly one of the most newest and flashiest street races with one of the most famous backdrops in the world after it took a spot on the F1 calendar in 2023, costing around $500 million.

The street circuit is one of few night races on the calendar, and includes the city's famous Strip and different landmarks around the city, such as the Bellagio and the Sphere.

The best place to watch the action unfold is from a casino, or West Harmon Zone grandstands. Casinos offer high-end packages to watch in specially built race zones around the circuit, but the grandstands around the final corner and viewing the pit straight still offer a great view.

Weather forecast

The weather for the Las Vegas Grand Prix is cold with temperatures between 10-14°C.

What happened last time out?

McLaren's Norris continued his impressive form in the business end of the season and put in a blistering lap to take pole position.

But come Sunday's race he ran wide at the first corner in an attempt to hold off Red Bull's Verstappen, who took advantage from second to gain the lead.

The Dutchman controlled the lead from that point onwards to win the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

Norris and Oscar Piastri ended up being disqualified from the race for a technical infringement -- a major blow in the title race with only two races to go at the time.

Who will win this year?

Mercedes completed the double and wrapped up the constructors' championship last time out, a week after Antonelli was crowned world champion.

With it being a night race, the conditions in Las Vegas are always very cold, a world away from some of the soaring temperatures the drivers race in throughout the year.

McLaren has been running a heavily-upgraded car that seems to be working well, and Norris will be carrying his winning momentum to Vegas.

Verstappen is in strong form and has made his way to second in the title standings with three victories under his belt and 12 podiums this year.

Having won twice in Vegas already, the Dutchman will certainly be the one to watch.

stories.headline: Sources: San Jose Earthquakes sold for $625 million to Heath Freeman
stories.summary: Alden Global Capital co-founder Heath Freeman is purchasing the San Jose Earthquakes from John Fisher, following MLS owners' approval of the sale Thursday.
stories.body:
The San Jose Earthquakes announced that Alden Global Capital co-founder Heath Freeman will acquire the team, as well as the club's home venue, PayPal Park, from John Fisher.

Sources confirmed a report from Sportico that the sale reflects an enterprise value of $625 million. The MLS board of governors unanimously approved the transfer of ownership Thursday, noting that the transaction will close in the coming weeks.

The deal will complete a lengthy sales process that began in June 2025. Investment bank Moelis helped facilitate the deal.

"My family and I are honored and humbled to be the next generation owners of the San Jose Earthquakes. I would like to thank John Fisher and the Fisher family for their confidence in me. I know how much they love this team and we expect to continue making them proud in this new era of the Quakes," Freeman said.

"Our vision is simple - winning on and off the field for San Jose and the entire region. The Bay Area is home to some of the world's great institutions, sports franchises and leaders. The standard has been set. We are eager to partner with and connect our community more closely with the Earthquakes and immerse them in our world."

The Quakes struggled during much of Fisher's tenure as owner, reaching the postseason just four times in the past 11 seasons. This season, under manager Bruce Arena, San Jose is in the MLS Cup Playoffs. It will face Houston Dynamo FC in Round 1 when it hosts Game 1 of the best-of-three series Nov. 24 at PayPal Park. The club won the 2012 Supporters' Shield.

"We are committed to investing in the team and building a club that consistently competes for championships," Freeman said. "Off the field, we are equally focused on strengthening our connections with fans and communities in San Jose and throughout the Bay Area. We believe the future of the Earthquakes is incredibly bright, and we can't wait to get started and take the Quakes to unforeseen heights."

Freeman has served as president of Alden Global Capital since 2014. He currently serves as chairman of Tribune Enterprises LLC, which owns and manages newspapers including the Chicago Tribune and South Florida Sun Sentinel, and as vice chairman of MNG Enterprises Inc., which manages newspapers such as The Denver Post, the Mercury News and the Boston Herald. Alden Global Capital has recently enacted deep cost cuts across its publications, leading to multiple layoffs.

Fisher has owned the Earthquakes since 2007, when he and Lew Wolff purchased an expansion team to replace the side that relocated to Houston after the 2005 season. During his tenure, he privately financed the construction of PayPal Park.

"My family and I have loved owning this club for almost 20 years and we are extremely grateful for the support of our amazing fans as well as the hard work of all of our coaches, players and staff," Fisher said. "We would like to thank Jared Shawlee and the executive staff for their leadership and the entire Quakes front office for their commitment to the club, the fans and the community."

"I want to thank John Fisher and his family for their nearly two decades of commitment to the San Jose Earthquakes, Major League Soccer and the Bay Area soccer community," said MLS commissioner Don Garber.

"John has been a great partner and a good friend, and his leadership and investment helped build a strong foundation for the club. Heath Freeman is an ambitious owner with a strong belief in the Earthquakes and the Bay Area as one of the country's great soccer markets. We are excited to welcome him to MLS and look forward to the energy and vision he will bring to this next chapter of the club."

Two MLS teams remain on the market. The Saputo family announced plans to sell CF Montréal earlier this week. The Vancouver Whitecaps are also still on the market, with Goldman Sachs leading that process.

BMO Capital Markets is managing the CF Montréal sale as lead financial adviser, with National Bank of Canada Capital Markets as co-adviser.

stories.headline: Despite injury and illness, Gus Teixeira is still one of this year's top prospects
stories.summary: Gus Teixeira spent much of his top-age year battling injury and illness, but still found a way to be in contention to be the top pick in the open pool, writes Japser Chellappah.
stories.body:
Gustavo Teixeira had a brilliant top-age campaign. He's worked his way into pick 1 conversations, and is locked into the first handful of selections on draft night.

His success is made all the more impressive considering what's played out behind the scenes.

"I had the ankle injury at the start of the year in the first praccy game," Teixeira tells ESPN.

"It was kind of a bit annoying because every week I thought I'd be playing but it just got pushed back. I had the calf injury, I was out for five or six weeks. I rehabbed that, played a game and then the foot pulled up sore and that's why I'm not testing [at the AFL Draft combine].

"I've also been sick for basically the whole year with a virus."

Teixeira, a powerful forward-half midfielder, played valiantly through glandular fever-like symptoms that didn't get diagnosed until the conclusion of the National Championships.

He was playing games deep in the forward 50 but still finding himself short of breath and unable to hit top gear. After being diagnosed with a severe iron deficiency and receiving an infusion he felt the energy he'd been lacking return, but not before a calf injury linked to his virus took Teixeira out for all but one game in the back half of the season.

Most top-10 chances at the AFL Draft thrive off injury-free seasons where they can continually put their name up in lights. Teixeira couldn't do that this year, so he made his moments count.

His first game back from an ankle concern was in a Vic Metro trial game where he showed his worth, kicking two goals from 20 disposals in a best afield display.

"It was a good day out, I was pretty happy with that. It was annoying I couldn't do a bit more of that throughout the year but I'm sure I can do that in the future."

Teixeira had locked himself into Metro's National Championships outfit by halftime, showing off the power and class that recruiters covet.

At the National Championships he was playing under duress from his undiagnosed virus, but he still took the opportunity to show his value deep in attack.

"Obviously I was sick so I was resting a bit, I was sore the first week and they wanted me to play more forward. I kicked a few goals and they wanted me to stay down forward and that's where I was able to impact the most," he tells ESPN.

Teixeira claimed All-Australian honours, booting seven goals in his four outings including a best on ground demolition of the Allies where he kicked four goals from 22 touches.

It was an element of his game that proved his worth outside of the centre square. Teixeira got to dangerous spots and created separation with proactive running, and from there was able to demonstrate his cleanliness and class to make his chances count.

"I've always thought I want to be a midfielder, I want to play in there. Skills are very important as a midfielder so you've got to be clean and you've got to be able to kick. I'm just chipping away at it and improving."

Teixeira is of Brazilian descent via his father Matt, who was born in the city of Belo Horizonte before moving to Australia when he was 25.

He brings Gus back to Brazil every year, and that connection to a non-English speaking country would allow Teixeira to join zoned club St Kilda's Next Generation Academy if not for friction points within the AFL's own NGA rules.

"Belo Horizonte is just inland of Rio... It's like the size of Melbourne but no one's really heard of it. It's a fully different culture and it's always great to go back," he explains.

"The AFL changed the rules for the regions this year, so they allow South American people this year but you need to be in it for three years. I would've only been in it for a year... my younger siblings are in it now. I've got a brother, Eddie, who's 12 and my sister Lucy who's 14."

Like a host of the top prospects this year, Teixeira has been an Essendon supporter his whole life. The Bombers have the top pick and Teixeira is within that bracket of the pool.

"I haven't thought about the Bombers pick-wise, but just the club and thinking about what it would be like obviously going to the Bombers, it'd be great at the moment. They're getting in some good coaches and they've got some good players coming through.

"Really though I'd be stoked to get drafted to any club, moving interstate would be a pretty cool experience. I'm always trying to get the best out of myself, I've always tried to be the best at everything and just put my best foot forward so I'll do that anywhere."

stories.headline: Kangaroos bounce Kiwis for fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup title
stories.summary: The Kangaroos have won a fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup, toppling New Zealand 32-12 in Brisbane.
stories.body:
The Kangaroos have punished a disappointing New Zealand, with Reece Walsh running riot in a 32-12 World Cup final waltz.

There was an expectation the Kiwis, searching for their second Cup title and first since 2008, would push Australia all the way after a two-point loss in a pulsating tournament opener.

But the visitors struggled from the outset in Brisbane on Sunday night, Jamayne Isaako's kick-off floating long in a sign of things to come.

Walsh dazzled at fullback for the Kangaroos, his pace, vision and wicked footwork too much as he helped lay on two tries and generally wreak havoc around the ruck and close to the line.

Conversely, Walsh's New Zealand opposite Kalyn Ponga -- International Rugby League's Golden Boot winner on Thursday night -- was unable to get into game.

Australian hooker Harry Grant and halves Tom Dearden and Cam Munster completely outplayed their error-riddled opposites, while the Kangaroos' pack muscled up.

Dearden laid on two first-half tries for Liam Martin with well-timed short balls, while Bradman Best was rewarded for an inspired chase-down tackle of Jahrome Hughes with a try soon after.

When Tom Trbojevic scored to begin the second half it was 28-6 and effectively game over.

Jack Bostock completed his breakout season with a try in each half for Australia.

It was the Kangaroos' fourth consecutive title and 10th in the last 11 tournaments, dating back to 1975.

stories.headline: Betting buzz: How improbable is this Browns season? Here's what the numbers say
stories.summary: Only 10 games into the season, the Cleveland Browns have already hit the over on their preseason win total, and that's just one of several notable numbers surrounding this team.
stories.body:
The Cleveland Browns have been an underdog going into every single one of their games this season except for one. They have trailed at some point in every game. Before the season, sportsbooks assigned them a win total of 5.5, tied for the third-lowest in the league, per DraftKings lines.

And yet, against all odds, the Browns are 6-4 more than halfway through the 2026 NFL season, becoming the first team in the league to hit the over on their preseason win total in the process.

Even more remarkably, all six of their wins have been in comeback fashion, with Sunday's victory over the Houston Texans serving as perhaps the finest example yet. Cleveland trailed 17-0 in the second quarter, at which point, their live odds to win the game lengthened all the way to +1480 on the live moneyline from a pregame closing line of +164, per DraftKings odds.

The Browns' latest cardiac accomplishment put them into rare air: They are the first team in NFL history to win their first six games by four points or fewer, and the first team in the Super Bowl era to be underdogs and win their first four home games, according to ESPN Research.

In each of those six wins, Cleveland has trailed at some point in the game, naturally forcing sportsbooks to lengthen their in-play odds and provide lucrative opportunities for bettors. Week 10's nearly 15-1 live line against Houston was the longest so far, but the Browns have been at least +365 at some point in every game, and were +1060 before coming back to beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in Week 2, per DraftKings lines.

"The Browns have turned live long shots into a weekly feature," Caesars Sportsbook's head of football Joey Feazel told ESPN over email. "Bettors are starting to recognize the pattern, and we have seen more interest in Cleveland when the Browns fall behind and their live price grows. There is still a little hesitation because repeatedly relying on fourth quarter comebacks is difficult, but bettors are becoming more willing to take a chance at the longer numbers."

To that point, Hard Rock Bet said that Cleveland's early season wins against the Carolina Panthers and Pittsburgh Steelers only attracted live ticket shares in the 30% range, but Sunday's latest victory got an 89% share.

The Browns are still a long shot to win the Super Bowl and AFC at 180-1 and 96-1, respectively, but other futures are starting to become more realistic, according to DraftKings odds movement. Cleveland entered the season at 21-1 to win the AFC North and have cut that almost in half to +1050, passing the preseason favorite Baltimore Ravens at 38-1.

Feazel says that Caesars has some liability on the Browns to win the division due to some "handsome prices," and BetMGM reported them as their third-most bet division winner since Week 1 by tickets. At both books, though, more bettors focused on Cleveland's win total under, allowing for a nice win relatively early in the season for the house.

Still, if the championship odds are any indication, bookmakers are not getting too ahead of themselves when approaching the Browns, noting that these miraculous wins, while entertaining, are not necessarily sustainable for long-term success.

"While our rating and view of the team is certainly well improved from what it was going into the season (they've already exceeded their preseason win total), we still do not view this as a top 20 team in the NFL from a power rating perspective," a senior NFL trader at Hard Rock Bet said in an email. "While their ability to win close games has certainly been impressive thus far, we expect some variance to swing the other way going forward in these results."

-- Doug Greenberg
