Nov. 1: Cardinals lead charge for big underdogs yet again

It has been a banner season for big underdogs in the NFL, as underdogs of seven or more points have won at least one game outright in each of the first eight weeks -- the first time that has happened since 1971, according to ESPN Research. Underdogs of at least seven points are now 20-7-2 against the spread (ATS) with nine straight-up wins.

Of all the big underdogs, though, one has stood above the rest: the Arizona Cardinals.

With their dramatic, come-from-behind overtime win against the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, the Cardinals notched their third outright victory of the season ... all of which have come when they were underdogs of seven or more points.

Arizona is the only team in the league to be 4-0 against the spread when coming in as an underdog of seven or more points and, oddly enough, their three ATS losses have come when they've been smaller underdogs (they have not been dubbed a favorite yet this season). They were responsible for the largest upset of the 2026 NFL season when they defeated the Los Angeles Rams as 13.5-point underdogs in Week 6.

In general, the big underdogs' winning and covering has been a welcome development for bookmakers: It's a well-known axiom in sports betting that the public tends to back favorites, both on the spread and as featured in moneyline parlays.

"Bettors still tend to be hesitant to trust big underdogs, which makes those occasional outright upsets especially valuable for the book," Caesars Sportsbook's head of football, Joey Feazel, told ESPN over email. "That has been a welcome change compared to 2024, when it often felt like the public's preferred teams continued to find a way home. Bettors are beginning to show more interest in taking the points with these underdogs, but we have not seen a widespread shift away from favorites on the moneyline just yet."

Feazel said that "Arizona was comfortably the most important decision in the book's favor" on Sunday, and DraftKings noted that neither team was heavily backed either way.

This most recent Cardinals win was particularly improbable. Down by 14 in the fourth quarter, Arizona was as long as 28-1 on DraftKings' live moneyline. Feazel said that some Caesars customers grabbed them in the 12-1 range, but not with significant enough money to cause too much of a problem for the sportsbook, while BetMGM called the Cardinals a "small loser" for the book due to live betting.

Seven-point underdogs trailing by 14 or more points in the fourth quarter are now 5-977 since 2000, according to ESPN Research. The Cardinals are also the first team in the Super Bowl era to have three road wins as at least seven-point underdogs in their first eight games.

Arizona began the season with the shortest odds to have the fewest regular-season wins (+250) and was tied with the Miami Dolphins with a preseason win total of 3.5, the lowest in the NFL since 2017. Less than halfway through the season, the Cardinals need just one more win to cash that futures ticket for faithful bettors.

Their first chance to do so will be in Week 9 when they go on the road to face the Seattle Seahawks ... as 11.5-point underdogs, per DraftKings lines.

-- Doug Greenberg

Oct. 23: Sportsbooks, bettors join the National Tight Ends Day frenzy

In 2018, the Supreme Court struck down the Professional and Amateur Sports Protection Act, clearing the way for states to legalize sports betting nationwide. That same year marked the beginning of another momentous occasion that has become a stalwart of NFL betting every season.

On the fourth Sunday in October -- Oct. 25 in 2026 -- the NFL celebrates National Tight Ends Day, a tongue-in-cheek commemoration of football's most underappreciated skill position. Since San Francisco 49ers tight ends Garrett Celek and George Kittle helped bring the honorary day to life eight years ago, it has become a staple of the betting world, with bookmakers taking extra notice and bettors staking extra cash backing players of the position.

"National Tight Ends Day has become a fun day for football fans, and we've seen the excitement around it grow each year," DraftKings director of sports operation Johnny Avello told ESPN via email. "This is a prime example of a way to have fun with the content on our platform."

The sportsbook noted that it sees more engagement on tight end player props on National Tight Ends Day than in any other week of a given season. On the day last season (Oct. 28), Hard Rock Bet says it saw tight ends account for 25% of all player prop selections compared to 11% the Sunday before and 9% the Sunday after. For touchdown scorer markets, that number jumped to 42% against 16% and 10% on the surrounding Sundays.

BetMGM specifically points out that its five most-bet players for props by tickets on the day in 2025 were all tight ends: Dallas Goedert, Tyler Warren, Tucker Kraft, Travis Kelce and Kittle.

Kraft celebrated by putting up a monster stat line of seven catches for 143 yards and two touchdowns in the Green Bay Packers' Week 8 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. Caesars Sportsbook head of football Joey Feazel said that "bettors certainly prospered" by backing Kraft and that the book has had to be more aware of bettor activity during this particular Sunday.

"This week certainly will increase the amount of action on tight ends in all facets of the games, which in turn has the ability to shorten touchdown prices when the amount of action is significantly increased," Feazel said via email. "But at the end of the day it will simply be the implied probability of each TE to score a touchdown."

Even with all the hype surrounding tight ends for the day, there are only four players with anytime touchdown odds shorter than +200, according to DraftKings odds as of Thursday evening: Brock Bowers (+110), Trey McBride (+130), Sam LaPorta (+170) and Kraft (+175). Those could -- and probably will -- change closer to kickoff as bettors pile on their favorite TEs and take advantage of the many promotions sportsbooks will be running for the occasion.

Sportsbooks, like Caesars, also plan to offer special markets, such as most tight end receiving yards, tight end touchdown combos and other milestone props. Last year, Hard Rock offered leaguewide touchdown ladders and a tight end to score in every Sunday 1 p.m. ET game (+1750), among other specialties.

You can find our bets for National Tight Ends Day here.

-- Doug Greenberg

Oct. 18: Cardinals pulls biggest upset of season, add to Rams' struggles

The Los Angeles Rams won over the betting public in the offseason and kicked off the regular season as the clear-cut Super Bowl favorites. They haven't lived up to that billing so far, suffering a new low Sunday.

The Rams lost to the Arizona Cardinals as 13.5-point home favorites in the biggest upset of the season based on point spread. They are only the second double-digit favorite to lose outright in the past two seasons, joining the Green Bay Packers, who lost to the Carolina Panthers in Week 9 last November as 13.5-point favorites.

Arizona's upset shredded survivor pool entries around the nation.

The Rams were picked by the most contestants in ESPN Survivor contests and in the high-stakes contests Circa Survivor and Circa Grandissimo in Las Vegas. Throw in the Indianapolis Colts' loss to the underdog and previously winless Tennessee Titans, and the Circa contests lost greater than 50% of the remaining entries.

The loss drops the Rams to 2-4 on the season, the same record as the Cardinals. The Rams are the second preseason Super Bowl favorite in the past 20 years to lose four of their first six games, per SportsOddsHistory.com. (The 2015 Seattle Seahawks started 2-4 and went on to lose in the divisional round of the playoffs.)

Los Angeles was favored to win the Super Bowl at 5-1 ahead of Week 1. No other team had Super Bowl odds shorter than 10-1. The Rams were +950 to win the Super Bowl on Sunday night at DraftKings, behind four teams.

More bets were placed and more money was wagered on the Rams to win the Super Bowl than any other team in the offseason at most sportsbooks.

-- David Purdum

Oct. 11: Who wants to win the NFC East?

Week 5 was one to forget for the NFC East, to say the least.

It started Thursday night when the Dallas Cowboys lost outright to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after closing as 8.5-point favorites, tied with four other games as the biggest upset of the season, according to DraftKings odds.

Not only were the Cowboys heavily backed on the spread and in moneyline parlays at multiple sportsbooks, they were also the most popular pick in both ESPN Survivor (40% of the remaining field) and the $1,000-per-entry Circa Survivor (2,554 entries, 42.8% of the remaining field). It's the third time in the season's first five weeks that ESPN Survivor's most popular pick lost.

But the misery didn't end there for the division. The Philadelphia Eagles led off the day in London by seemingly notching a winning field goal with eight seconds left against the Jacksonville Jaguars, giving them a 99.5% chance to win the game, per ESPN Analytics.

Jacksonville returned the ensuing kickoff to the Philadelphia 35-yard line with one second left, allowing the Jags to kick a winning field goal as time expired. It was the first game in the Super Bowl era that featured two go-ahead field goals in the final 10 seconds of the fourth quarter, according to ESPN Research.

Then, there was the most bizarre result of the week, possibly the season. The New York Giants and Washington Commanders played a mistake-ridden game into an overtime where neither team scored, including in the matchup's final moments when the Commanders somehow ran out the clock while in field goal range.

"In the closing minutes and overtime, the live moneyline market was in complete chaos," Joey Feazel, Caesars Sportsbook head of football, told ESPN via email. "Every big play looked like it might decide the game and the book's fate, only for the final whistle to leave everyone staring at the screen wondering what had just happened. It was 90-plus minutes of drama, countless swings in perceived win probability, and in the end, nobody got the outcome they were expecting."

That's right: None of the NFC East teams recorded a win in Week 5 ... despite two of the teams playing each other.

Going into "Thursday Night Football," the Cowboys had been the +105 favorites to win the division and immediately dropped to +164 following their upset loss, tying them with the Eagles. After Week 5, Philadelphia is now the slight favorite for the division at +170 -- the longest odds for any division favorite in the league. Next comes Dallas at +180, followed by current division leader New York at +320 and Washington at +750. All of the teams in the NFC East show underdog plus-odds to make the playoffs ... even though one of them has to.

The Eagles had actually been a top-six favorite for the Super Bowl at 17-1 going into the season, but that number has lengthened to 40-1. The Cowboys are now the Super Bowl favorite among NFC East teams at 30-1 after coming into the season at 25-1.

The whole situation is made all the more disorienting by the fact that bettors had much higher expectations for this division going into the season. At BetMGM, Dallas is the biggest liability for the NFC championship, having attracted a $10,000 wager at 16-1 odds to win $160,000.

The Giants provoked a $5,000 wager to win the Super Bowl at 66-1 odds, creating a potential payout of $330,000. New York is also the largest liability to win the NFC East at both BetMGM and DraftKings, with both books also reporting some action for the division on Dallas.

"The Eagles/Commanders right now are the best-case scenario for the book with the Giants/Cowboys being the best-case scenario for the bettors," Feazel said, "but based on today's events we are not sure that any of these teams would like to win the division."

-- Doug Greenberg

Sept. 28: Betting buzz: 8.5 the magic number for underdogs

Big underdogs are having a historic start to the 2026 NFL season, and it's all revolving around one number.

On Sunday, the Washington Commanders upset the reigning Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks after coming into the matchup as 8.5-point underdogs. In Week 2, the New Orleans Saints defeated the Baltimore Ravens outright as 8.5-point underdogs and the Cleveland Browns beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers as underdogs by the same number. And in Week 1, the Arizona Cardinals pulled off the first big upset of the season when they defeated the Los Angeles Chargers ... again, as 8.5-point underdogs.

The four straight-up wins by underdogs of eight points or greater is the most through three weeks of a season since 1978 when five teams accomplished the feat, according to ESPN Research.

Only one 8.5-point favorite has survived so far: the Jacksonville Jaguars, who won and covered against the Browns in Week 1. Additionally, the only two favorites of greater than 8.5 -- the San Francisco 49ers (-12.5) in Week 2 and the Kansas City Chiefs (-10) in Week 3 -- also won and covered, both against the Miami Dolphins.

Because public bettors generally like to back big favorites -- via straight spread wagers, teasers or money-line parlays -- the underdog wins have been a boon to sportsbooks. At DraftKings, Washington's outright win against Seattle during Week 3 was "a good outcome for the book" after the Seahawks became the sportsbook's fourth-most-backed team of the day, pushing the line up from 6.5 earlier in the week, according to a sportsbook representative.

"The Commanders' win was the most impactful result for the book," Caesars Sportsbook head of football Joey Feazel told ESPN over email. "The news throughout the week created a perfect storm for bettors to focus on Seattle. With Sam Darnold returning and Marcus Mariota starting for Washington, the Seahawks became the perceived 'free square' in parlays."

Through "Sunday Night Football," underdogs are 7-8 outright in Week 3. If the Chicago Bears win Monday night, it will be the first time that underdogs have gone .500 or better in a week since Week 5 of 2025, according to ESPN Research based on DraftKings odds.

For the third time in as many weeks this NFL season, the big underdog win also meant carnage for survivor pools: Seattle was the third-most selected team in ESPN Survivor with 11% of the picks, and the second-most selected in Circa Survivor at 12.9%.

Lawrence's costly kneel
With nearly nine minutes remaining in the Jacksonville Jaguars' blowout win over the New England Patriots, quarterback Trevor Lawrence pulled a bizarre move when he took a knee at the 1-yard line, allowing running back Bhayshul Tuten to score on the next play. Lawrence's kneel cost his fantasy owners and benefited Tuten's, but some bettors in Florida really paid the price.

At Hard Rock Sportsbook, Lawrence's odds to score a touchdown settled at +275 before the game and several bettors included him in long-shot parlays. One such parlay saw the first seven legs hit, and missed out on Lawrence getting in the endzone as the eighth and final leg. The $10 ticket would have paid out $11,323.72.

Another saw a $2,000 five-leg parlay hit on only four of its legs, including Lawrence over 16.5 rushing yards, but missed on Lawrence anytime touchdown, denying a $33,339.20 payday. Ouch.

Chi-Town quarterback shuffle
Six points -- that's how much the betting market believes the difference between Chicago Bears QB Caleb Williams and third-string QB Case Keenum, who is expected to start when the Philadelphia Eagles visit Soldier Field on Monday.

The Bears were 1.5-point favorites over the Eagles in the early lines posted last week, before Williams went down with a leg injury in Week 2's game against the Minnesota Vikings.

The line reopened at Eagles -4.5 on Monday, dropped to -3 during the week as hopes of Williams being able to return surfaced. But Williams was ruled out Sunday and Keenum was named the expected starter. The line settled back at -4.5 on Sunday.

Sportsbooks reported around 75% of the bets and money wagered on the Monday night game had been on the favored Eagles.

-- Doug Greenberg and David Purdum

stories.headline: Toronto Tempo win 2027 WNBA draft lottery, land No. 1 pick
stories.summary: The Tempo won the WNBA draft lottery on Sunday night, earning the No. 1 pick and potentially the chance to draft USC star JuJu Watkins. The Comets will choose second, followed by the Mystics.
stories.body:
The Toronto Tempo will have the No. 1 pick in the 2027 WNBA draft after winning the draft lottery Sunday night.

After completing its inaugural season in 2026, Toronto becomes the first franchise to have the top pick heading into its second season since the Dream in 2009, when Atlanta selected Angel McCoughtry. The Tempo will make their selection on April 12.

Lottery odds are based on teams' two-year cumulative records, except for Portland and Toronto, which were expansion teams in 2026. Their odds were solely based on their records from this past season.

The Houston Comets, formerly the Connecticut Sun (22-66), and Toronto (11-33) had the best odds to land the No. 1 pick, each with 329 chances out of 1,000. This marked the first time since 2015 that two teams had the same odds for the first overall selection.

The Sun, relocating to Texas from Connecticut this offseason, went 1-2 against Toronto in 2026 -- which is the first tiebreaker -- so the franchise couldn't fall further than the third pick. Toronto was guaranteed at least the fourth selection.

"I (felt) like something amazing was going to happen," said Tempo forward Aneesah Morrow, the team's lottery representative. "We're here now ... The future is bright. We have great and amazing players, and we have a country on our back. It feels different when you play like that."

Houston will select second in the draft. All of the other draft picks are in line with what the odds projected heading into Sunday. Washington, which had the next-best odds since acquiring Chicago's first-round pick in the trade that sent Ariel Atkins to the Sky, will pick third.

Seattle will select at No. 4, followed by Portland at No. 5. The Los Angeles Sparks have the sixth and seventh picks -- one that is their own and the other acquired from Phoenix in the Kelsey Plum trade in August.

USC's JuJu Watkins is projected to go No. 1 in ESPN's latest mock draft released Thursday, with Texas' Madison Booker slotted in at No. 2.

Notre Dame's Hannah Hidalgo, Virginia's Kymora Johnson, LSU's Mikaylah Williams, Kansas' S'Mya Nichols and Sarah Cisse of France are projected to round out the lottery picks.

The Tempo had a strong start to their season before veteran Brittney Sykes was sidelined indefinitely with a plantar fascia injury. After she went down, Toronto went 4-21, including a 12-game losing streak. But Sykes and Marina Mabrey combined to form one of the highest-scoring backcourts in the league.

Toronto has some young talent in Morrow, whom the team acquired in a midseason trade, and last year's No. 6 pick Kiki Rice. Rice was the team's third-leading scorer, but missed nearly two months with a Grade 2 left ankle sprain. The combination of Mabrey, Sykes and Rice gives the Tempo depth on the perimeter, however they are lacking as many options in the front court.

"(Toronto) is amazing," Morrow said. "Ever since I walked in the locker room, from the beginning, I was able to see the chemistry ... it's all about building the future of the Toronto franchise."

The 2027 season will also see the schedule increase from 44 to 50 games, making it the longest WNBA season in league history. The expanded footprint was allowed under the new collective bargaining agreement -- which also vastly increased pay, secured a $2.2 billion media deal and slated six expansion teams to join the league between 2024 and 2030.

The 2027 WNBA season is expected to start May 7 and has a latest possible end date of Oct. 24, sources told ESPN's Alexa Philippou last week.

"We're excited about the momentum -- it's never been stronger," said Bethany Donaphin, senior vice president and head of WNBA league operations. "We think there's a demand and we're excited to expand to 50 games."

The rest of the first-round draft order is: No. 8 New York, No. 9 Dallas, No. 10 Indiana, No. 11 Chicago, No. 12 Chicago, No. 13 Dallas, No. 14 Golden State and No. 15 Minnesota.

stories.headline: Hawks erase 22-point second quarter deficit to hand Bucks 10th consecutive loss
stories.summary: — Nickeil Alexander-Walker and CJ McCollum each scored 20 points and Onyeka Okongwu had 16 and 11 rebounds as the Atlanta Hawks erased a 22-point second-quarter deficit to defeat the Milwaukee Bucks 113-106 on Sunday night.
stories.body:
MILWAUKEE -- — Nickeil Alexander-Walker and CJ McCollum each scored 20 points and Onyeka Okongwu had 16 and 11 rebounds as the Atlanta Hawks erased a 22-point second-quarter deficit to defeat the Milwaukee Bucks 113-106 on Sunday night.


Jalen Johnson added 14 points and 11 rebounds and Corey Kispert had 14 off the bench for the Hawks (8-6), who had lost back-to-back games coming in.


Kasparas Jakucionis scored a career high 25 points, Gary Trent Jr. had 18, Kyle Kuzma 14 and Brayden Burries 13 for Milwaukee.


The Bucks (1-13) lost a 10th straight game and are off to their worst start in 52 years, when they lost 13 of their first 14 in 1974-75 without an injured Kareem Abdul-Jabbar, per Sportradar.


Milwaukee’s last win came on Oct. 26 against the Indiana Pacers in Milwaukee. The longest losing streak in franchise history is 15 consecutive games, set during the 1995-96 season.


The Bucks sprinted to a 37-18 lead after the first quarter, led by Kuzma’s 12 points. Milwaukee shot 58% in the period.


Milwaukee built a 22-point lead early in the second quarter before Atlanta stormed back to take a 55-53 lead at the half on Dyson Daniels’ layup just ahead of the horn.


The Hawks extended their run in the third, getting the lead up to 13, and holding an 87-80 lead heading the fourth.


The Bucks were within three with under a minute left but McCollum's jumper with 17 seconds left sealed the win.


Jock Landale (right hip inflammation) sat out for the Hawks, while the Bucks were without Ryan Rollins (illness) and Ousmane Dieng, who is set to have surgery Monday on a left finger he fractured in Friday’s loss at Orlando.


Up next
Hawks: At Oklahoma City on Wednesday night.


Bucks: At Miami on Wednesday night.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Will Bruno Fernandes stay put at Man United?
stories.summary: Bruno Fernandes' future at Manchester United is reportedly uncertain with his contract expiring next summer. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is holding off on signing a new contract for now, while Arsenal are the latest team to join a long list of admirers following Middlesbrough striker Will Lankshear. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes is holding off on signing a new contract for now, says The Sun. Fernandes, 32, has a contract which expires next summer -- albeit with a one-year club option to renew -- and reportedly wants to wait to see what happens under new boss Mauricio Pochettino. The Portugal midfielder has been linked with a lucrative move to Saudi Arabia before.

- Arsenal are in the market for a center forward, and TEAMtalk claims that the Gunners are the latest team to join a long list of admirers following Middlesbrough striker Will Lankshear. The 21-year-old joined Boro from Tottenham Hotspur this summer, after a loan spell at Oxford United in the Championship, and has hit the ground running, scoring 13 goals in as many appearances in the league so far. That has brought about plenty of transfer interest, but Middlesbrough will try to block any exit in January.

- Arsenal are continuing the push to sign a left-sided forward, with RB Leipzig star Antonio Nusa leading their shortlist, says TEAMtalk. Gabriel Martinelli and Leandro Trossard left in the summer, and were replaced by Christos Tzolis before a move to sign Vinícius Júnior from Real Madrid fell short. With Mikel Arteta wanting more options on that flank, the report claims that talks have opened with Nusa's representatives about a possible switch, but the 21-year-old's transfer could cost €80 million.

- Tottenham defender Pedro Porro has decided that he only wants to join Barcelona if he leaves the club, according to Sport. The 27-year-old Spain right back has seen interest from the Blaugrana, as well as Real Madrid, despite only signing a new contract with Spurs in the summer. But while Barcelona are eyeing up a deal worth no more than €50 million next summer, Tottenham will stand firm on their €70 million valuation.

- AC Milan are looking to bolster in the forward areas during January, with Gazzetta dello Sport reporting that Real Madrid's Endrick and Club Brugge's Nicolò Tresoldi are on their shortlist. Endrick has seen few minutes in the starting XI for Los Blancos this season and Milan are keen on a loan deal with a permanent option included. Meanwhile, Tresoldi 22, who has five goals in four Champions League appearances this season, has caught the eye of a number of a teams and could move in a €60 million deal.

Other rumors
- Arsenal believe that Real Madrid forward Vinicius Junior will join the club eventually. (Football Transfers)

- Sunderland will look to block any move for Brian Brobbey, as Tottenham are eyeing a potential deal for the striker. (Football Insider)

- Liverpool, Real Madrid and AC Milan are set to face off for the signature of Angelo Stiller, with the VfB Stuttgart midfielder attracting interest heading into January. (Ekrem Konur)

- Liverpool would be willing to trigger the €55 million permanent clause in Ronald Araújo's contract this January, but the Barcelona defender's loan only includes the option for the end of the season. The 27-year-old has been a regular at right back for the Reds since joining on loan in the summer. (Marca)

- Borussia Mönchengladbach attacking midfielder Wael Mohya, 17, is now attracting interest from Liverpool, Real Madrid, Barcelona, Bayern Munich and AC Milan after a breakthrough season in the Bundesliga. (Ekrem Konur)

- Versatile midfielder Brian Fariñas is set to extend his contract with Barcelona, as the 20-year-old holds new talks with sporting director Deco. The Spaniard has featured three times for the Blaugrana so far this season, and has filled in at full back. (Marca)

- Two clubs outside of Serie A have been enquiring about the future of Juventus winger Edon Zhegrova, with the 27-year-old Kosovo international facing a potential exit in January. (Nicolò Schira)

- Juventus remain keen on signing striker Alexander Sørloth from Atlético Madrid, after failing in their pursuit in the summer. Discussions have already been held about a deal for the 30-year-old. (La Gazzetta dello Sport)

- Juventus are also keeping a close eye on Hakan Çalhanoğlu, as his contract situation with Inter Milan unravels. The Old Lady remain keen on the 32-year-old midfielder, who is a free agent next summer, while talks over a new deal have seemingly stalled. (Tuttosport)

stories.headline: Blue Jays' Anthony Santander apologizes for sharing anti-Muslim posts
stories.summary: Blue Jays outfielder Anthony Santander apologized for sharing anti-Muslim social media posts, saying it caused hurt and fell short of his own convictions.
stories.body:
Toronto Blue Jays outfielder Anthony Santander apologized Friday for sharing anti-Muslim social media posts, saying the content caused hurt and fell short of his own convictions.

In a statement on Instagram, Santander said reflection and conversations with people he trusts made him recognize that he should have been more thoughtful about what he shared and the responsibility that comes with having a public voice.

"I realize that this content caused hurt and I sincerely apologize," Santander said in his statement.

He expressed respect for the Muslim community and pledged to avoid sharing content that promotes hate.

"As a man of faith, it is my belief that every person deserves to be treated with dignity and respect, regardless of their religion, background, or beliefs," Santander said. "After hearing feedback from those I hurt, I realize that the content I shared fell short of my own convictions."

Santander shared the posts Nov. 4 and deleted them the next morning, including a video of a Christian preacher disparaging Muslims and another suggesting Sharia law would be imposed on the United States after Abdul El-Sayed's election to the Senate in Michigan.

His apology came a day after Blue Jays president and chief executive officer Mark Shapiro apologized to the Muslim community and fans following a meeting with community leaders, and after general manager Ross Atkins asked Santander to publicly address the controversy.

The 32-year-old Venezuelan player signed a $92.5 million, five-year contract with Toronto in January 2025 but missed the entire 2026 season because of injuries. It remains unclear whether the team will discipline him over the posts.

stories.headline: Gane deserves a home fight; Nunes fought right into Harrison's hands
stories.summary: Ciryl Gane deserves a chance to win over fans, while Amanda Nunes fought the wrong fight against Kayla Harrison.
stories.body:
Ciryl Gane has become accustomed to being the villain, even after some of the biggest performances of his career. But after another successful title defense -- a unanimous decision victory over Josh Hokit at UFC 334 in New York on Saturday -- maybe it's time for the UFC to give its heavyweight champion a different kind of reception. A fight in his home country could be exactly what he needs.

In the co-main event, Amanda Nunes had the experience and striking ability to give Kayla Harrison a difficult night. But instead of forcing Harrison to fight on her terms, Nunes played into the reigning champion's greatest strength. The result was a costly tactical mistake that ultimately decided the fight.

Brett Okamoto and Jeff Wagenheim give their takeaways from the two title fights.

UFC should book Gane a fight in France

UFC heavyweight champion Gane has been the recipient of a lot of boos over the past several years. I feel it's time to change that.

If you believe Gane has brought those boos on himself, that's understandable. He looked flat and almost intimidated in a loss to Jon Jones in 2023. His questionable decision-making might have cost him a win against Francis Ngannou in 2022. Tom Aspinall remains unable to compete after Gane poked him in the eye during their 2025 title fight. And his biggest win to date, a second-round finish of Alex Pereira in June, was somewhat marred by Pereira's accusation that Gane landed blows to the back of his head.

UFC CEO Dana White suggested as much during the postfight news conference Saturday. He said he believes Gane receives an appropriate amount of respect for his accomplishments, and any of the criticisms he has received -- well, he did all those aforementioned things.

But Gane also dug deep Saturday and turned away a hungry title challenger in Josh Hokit -- and was booed for it. He landed the most strikes in a single heavyweight bout in UFC history, but some fans might be talking about Hokit getting robbed of a decision Monday morning.

I would like to see the UFC look for an opportunity to put Gane in a position to be celebrated, not booed. He deserves that. Gane has built an impressive résumé that makes him one of the best pound-for-pound fighters in the world. For the past year, he has played the role of a calm, unbothered villain. I'd like to see what it looks like -- what he looks like -- in a different environment, like fighting in his home country of France. - Okamoto

Nunes was beaten by the wrong game plan

Kayla Harrison fought a Kayla Harrison fight. Amanda Nunes? She fought a Kayla Harrison fight, too.

I bet you can guess who is better at fighting a Kayla Harrison fight.

Harrison made her first defense of the UFC women's bantamweight title a success by dominating the grappling, which is no surprise considering she is a two-time Olympic judo gold medalist who has been a force on the canvas since transitioning to MMA. The only surprise is that Nunes was so willing to veer from the striking, where she held a distinct advantage, and venture into Harrison's wheelhouse.

Nunes had been away from the sport for 3½ years and is 38 years old, so going into the fight, it would have been reasonable to assume that her physical skills would be diminished. That did not appear to be the case. Instead, her game plan did her in.

If anything, Nunes gave future Harrison opponents a blueprint of what not to do against the champion -- and, yes, a few fleeting glimpses of where they might take advantage of Harrison, whose striking is rudimentary at best. Whoever steps in to challenge Harrison next will have to figure out a way to stay on their feet. Good luck with that. -- Wagenheim

stories.headline: How Kimi Antonelli overcame George Russell, Ferrari to become F1's youngest champion
stories.summary: How Kimi Antonelli overcame early setbacks, teammate George Russell and a Ferrari fightback to become Formula 1's youngest-ever world champion.
stories.body:
Kimi Antonelli was crowned the 2026 Formula 1 world champion at the Mexico City Grand Prix, sealing the title with four races of the season remaining.

He stood on the last step of the podium, behind race winner Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton in the Ferrari.

At 20 years old, Antonelli made his title fight look remarkably easy. He laid down the foundations with his maiden victory at the second race of the season in China, and with the exception of the occasional reliability setback with his Mercedes, he remained composed ever since.

It marked Mercedes' return to the top winning its first drivers' and constructors' trophy since Hamilton six years ago, and the team have well and truly unlocked their next superstar -- a superstar simply just enjoying himself.

Here are the highs -- and few low points -- that shaped his title-winning campaign.

- Kimi Antonelli makes F1 history as youngest world champion with maiden title

- Kimi Antonelli's historic F1 title: Every record broken and milestone reached

- In pictures: The moments that defined Kimi Antonelli's F1 title-winning season

Melbourne crash, early favourite Russell wins opener
It was George Russell, not Antonelli, who was the name on everyone's lips coming into the season. Russell was one of the standout performers in 2025, while Antonelli's rookie season had been a rollercoaster. When it was clear Mercedes was the team to beat, Russell was the easy pick for the title.

By the time the season-opener had arrived in Melbourne, it was clear he had finally got what he dreamt of after a tedious four-year wait -- a fast and dominant Mercedes to match his ambition. It was an opportunity he couldn't afford to waste.

To anyone who had paid attention to 2025, it was perhaps not surprising how the opening weekend went. Antonelli showed flashes of pace but a crash in final practice left him on the back foot going into qualifying. TV cameras showed Toto Wolff and his race engineer Peter Bonnington comforting a disconsolate Antonelli after the smash.

Russell claimed pole, although Mercedes' quick repair job allowed Antonelli to get out and lock out the front row of the grid. The race was a showcase of F1's new era. F1's 2026 hybrid engine regulations featured a near 50/50 split between internal combustion and electrical power, but it was instantly met with driver criticism with Max Verstappen labelling them "anti-racing."

At the start of the race, Russell powered down to Turn 1 in a comfortable lead, but a sluggish start for Antonelli followed -- something that would be an early theme of his season. He quickly fought back through the order. A thrilling back and forth contest followed, as Ferrari briefly fought Mercedes for the win, but by the end it was as they were at the beginning -- Russell winning, although he had not been able to shake Antonelli, who finished just under three seconds behind.

Russell seemed overjoyed at the start.

"I love this car, I love this engine!" Russell declared over the radio after the race.

As for Antonelli, the young Italian had managed to avoid the disaster of his practice crash, but he was still tellingly hard on himself afterwards. To team boss Wolff, it was the kind of baptism by fire he expected the Italian would have in his sophomore season now the team was the benchmark car to beat.

"He's literally learning [F1] the hard way, which makes him stronger," Wolff commented on Antonelli after the race. "He was very, very strong on Friday and his pace on Saturday was there. But then the accident happened, and that can happen."

But anyone who thought the opening race of the season was a sign of things to come was gravely mistaken.

Championship standings after Australia:

Russell -- 25

Antonelli -- 18

China breakthrough changes everything
Mercedes showed the first glimpses of vulnerability in China with a series of front wing and technical problems, but it was not enough to stop another lockout of the front row. This time, Antonelli did not repeat any of his Melbourne mistakes, claiming a resounding first career pole position -- becoming the youngest driver in history to do so.

Antonelli had another sluggish getaway though, and after trying to cover Russell into Turn 1, the Mercedes drivers both allowed Hamilton's Ferrari to swoop into an early lead. Mercedes' strong pace quickly showed itself and Antonelli got back ahead a lap later, the beginning of a dominant and assured drive to his first win. It made him F1's second youngest winner of all time, behind Verstappen.

"I'm speechless," an emotional Antonelli said after the race. "I'm about to cry, to be honest. Thank you so much to my team, because they helped me to achieve this dream."

For anyone who had already handed Russell the title after Melbourne, Antonelli's Shanghai drive seemed to be a clear reminder the Brit would not have it all his own way.

It had been a monumental weekend for Antonelli with landmark pole and wins. A week later, he did the same again and took pole at the Japanese Grand Prix, with Russell nearly three-tenths behind. Again, Antonelli struggled at the start, dropping to sixth by the end of the first lap as Oscar Piastri and Charles Leclerc battled for the lead, with Russell fourth. The pendulum of the race seemed to be swinging back to Russell as he carved through the field, but a pit stop on lap 22 from the lead would prove his undoing. Almost immediately afterwards, Oliver Bearman crashed at Spoon, triggering a safety car.

It was manna from heaven for Antonelli, who effectively got a free pit stop, vaulting him up the order and ahead of Russell and Piastri.

"Unbelievable!" said Russell on his radio immediately afterwards.

Russell dropped to fourth by the end, a quite remarkable outcome for such a dominant car. Out in front, Antonelli surged clear, winning over Piastri by a dominant 17 seconds. Antonelli might have been fortuitous getting to the lead, but there was nothing lucky about the margin of victory: Antonelli was looking every bit worthy of his newest accolade and the youngest man to ever lead the world championship. Little did anyone know it then, but it was a lead he would never relinquish.

He would have several weeks to dwell on the new place in the history books, too, with the outbreak of war in Iran cancelling April's races in Bahrain and Saudi Arabia.

Championship standings after Japan:

Antonelli -- 72

Russell -- 63

Three wins that broke Russell's challenge
The next three races underlined Antonelli's superiority and marked what would be the turning point in the season. Russell was no longer the established team leader waiting for the next generation to catch up -- Antonelli was in fact fully caught up. After the break caused by the Middle East cancellations -- Bahrain was subsequently moved to Malaysia in September -- Russell looked to fight back in Miami and the sprint appeared to suggest the title battle would swing back and forth. Antonelli out-qualified Russell comfortably but his Achilles heel from the year quickly re-emerged as he fluffed his start and dropped down the order. Norris and Piastri claimed a McLaren one-two while Russell was fourth and Antonelli sixth.

The momentum would swing again hours later. In qualifying again the difference between the pair was clear as Antonelli romped to his third straight pole position, with Russell languishing down in fifth. The young Italian's race start got the better of him once again and he ran wide at Turn 1 while Leclerc took a comfortable lead.

Antonelli and Leclerc fought out in front before Norris came into the mix and headed the field on lap 14. It was Antonelli vs. Norris for the rest of the race, before the Italian fended off the reigning world champion to take his third win in a row.

"This is just the beginning," Antonelli declared afterwards. "The road is still long, but we're working super hard and the team is doing an incredible job."

Canada followed and would deliver a blockbuster moment between the Mercedes duo. It was a Russell stronghold -- three pole positions to his name and a victory the year prior, the perfect place to kick life into his stuttering campaign. Russell started perfectly, taking a comfortable sprint pole, with Norris ahead of Antonelli in third. The mini-race featured a tense battle between the pair, with Antonelli being forced wide while trying a very ambitious move around the outside at Turn 1.

The Italian driver would then lose second after going wide a lap later while trying to pass Russell, losing second to Norris. Antonelli was fuming on the radio, leading to an intervention from Wolff. "Kimi, concentrate on the driving please, and not on the radio moaning," he said. Russell knew this weekend was his time to shine and he ended up stamping his authority and producing another stunning pole, but the race couldn't have gone any worse.

Both Mercedes drivers had a poor start while Norris took the lead before being called into the pits. Antonelli and Russell had fierce wheel-to-wheel battles for the best part of 27 laps, providing some excellent entertainment. Neither driver was willing to give an inch -- it seemed like all of Mercedes' worst nightmares coming back to life, with memories of Hamilton and Nico Rosberg's collisions in 2014 and 2016 while fighting each other for championships.

Fate would intervene before Russell and Antonelli were able to create another, with Russell retiring from the lead with a reliability issue while fending off his younger teammate. "It feels like the gods don't want me to be in this fight," a deflated Russell would say later. Antonelli's win rubbed salt into the wounds.

The Brit needed a clean weekend at the Monaco Grand Prix, but instead the problems continued. He qualified in sixth while Antonelli started on pole at a circuit where overtaking is notoriously difficult.

Monaco felt like a sucker punch to Russell. This time, Antonelli was flawless, taking a great pole. Antonelli's launch off the line was strong, but chaos unfolded behind him. In a race filled with incidents, Safety Cars and a red flag. Russell would be one of the drivers given a drive-through penalty for a minor pit-lane speeding infraction -- one later revealed to have been caused by the FIA incorrectly measuring pit entry. During a red flag, Russell argued his penalty should be deferred to after the race, but he served the drive-through anyway, dropping to the back.

Antonelli's win gave him another unanswered 25 points -- 50 in two races. While Canada had shown the raw side of Antonelli, Monaco had shown his class. Russell's championship hopes were slowly slipping from his grasp.

Championship standings after Monaco:

Antonelli -- 156

Russell -- 88

Ferrari fightback puts Antonelli under pressure
A team in red decided to join the title party and arrived to the Barcelona-Catalunya Grand Prix with its first major upgrade -- and suddenly Mercedes had a title challenger.

Russell responded to his title struggles with pole, while Hamilton split the two Mercedes' to start the race second. A perfectly executed three-stop strategy played into the seven-time world champion's hands to make history and win his first race with the Scuderia, becoming the first driver of the season to end Mercedes' winning streak.

Antonelli suffered an electrical shutdown and was forced to retire from second place with just four laps remaining, while Russell gained some much-needed points in the title race. Hamilton cut the gap in the championship to Antonelli by 41 points -- making him a worthy title contender.

Antonelli lost 18 points in the championship and was downcast afterwards. He said: "I feel very empty emotionally right now, because we're trying to soak in what has just happened."

Russell arrived to Austria ready to fight back and locked out the front-row in what was a controversial pole position which occurred during a yellow flag period. He converted his pole into his second race win by nearly three-tenths from Antonelli, who stood on the final spot of the podium.

There might have been a glimpse of hope for Russell who said afterwards that he was "feeling like himself again." But that euphoric feeling was followed by a kick in the teeth at the next race when Antonelli bounced back at the British Grand Prix. He edged out Hamilton to win the sprint race after making a move on lap 8 of 17 from second. He crossed the line 2.7 seconds clear of Hamilton, with Norris third and Russell fourth.

The Italian took his form into the rest of the weekend with a stunning pole ahead of Leclerc. But during the race, it was the Ferrari man who had a mighty launch off the line to take the lead and win his first race in two years.

For Antonelli it was a race to forget as he scrambled for a point in ninth and desperately pleaded on the Mercedes team radio to stay out on track to seal a singular championship point. He was then demoted to 16th following a time penalty for exceeding track limits when he was struggling with car reliability.

It was a mixed bag of results for Mercedes, while Ferrari continued to build momentum. With the summer races in full swing, the championship fight was far from over.

Championship standings after Silverstone:

Antonelli -- 179

Russell -- 154

Hamilton -- 147

Antonelli strikes back

Russell's fightback did not last long. At Spa-Francorchamps, Antonelli got things back on track, claiming pole with a scintillating lap 0.3 seconds quicker than Norris in second, while Russell had to settle for fourth. The first lap seemed to be another of the micromoments which summed up Russell's year. Already starting down on Antonelli, Russell's electrical boost did not materialize in time for the Eau Rouge/Kemmel Straight on the opening lap.

Starved of power, Russell was swallowed up by other cars into Les Combes, tangling with Hamilton's Ferrari and ending in the gravel. "I'm out," Russell said on radio immediately after finishing. "What the f--- happened down the straight? I had no battery down the straight! Unacceptable! Unf------g acceptable!" If there was ever a radio message which summed up his mood and his season, Russell had delivered it. All of his hard work of the past handful of races, the gentle chipping away at Antonelli, was undone like that. Out in front, Antonelli briefly lost the lead to Verstappen, but soon got himself back in front to romp home to another comprehensive win.

Russell's engine issues would emerge again at the start of the Hungarian Grand Prix, as he struggled to get away and dropped from the third row of the grid to the back of the field. Out in front, McLaren's Norris capitalized on teammate Piastri's late race retirement to win.

Going into the summer break, Hamilton appeared to be just as big a threat to Antonelli's championship as Russell.

Championship standings after Belgium:

Antonelli -- 204

Hamilton -- 159

Russell -- 154

Forza Kimi!

Formula 1's summer break ended with the last Dutch Grand Prix to be held at Zandvoort under its current deal. Russell came into the second half of the season promising an all-or-nothing approach to his teammate's title lead and took sprint pole and then sprint victory to kick the season off in positive form.

The pendulum would swing back Antonelli's way the following day. Antonelli got the jump on Russell at the start before Verstappen crashed uncharacteristically on a wet-dry track. Antonelli briefly got ahead of Norris at the restart, but soon dropped behind the McLaren driver again. A late Virtual Safety Car gave Mercedes a dilemma. Antonelli pitted for fresh tyres to cover the threat of the looming Ferrari drivers, but rejoined behind Russell, who had stayed out on older tyres. Antonelli was quicker but also being caught by the two Ferraris. Mercedes immediately intervened, asking Russell to let Antonelli by into second position. Russell would oblige, despite a muted objection on the radio, and held off Hamilton to complete a double podium for Mercedes. It was odd to see a driver move over for a title rival, but showed how well Mercedes had managed the intra-team dynamic.

Rather than it becoming a controversy, Russell defended the call post-race. He said: "I mean, Kimi was ahead of me anyway. He deserved to finish ahead ... That's always just been our sort of rules, and the fact is Kimi was ahead of me before the VSC [Virtual Safety Car], and he tried something different to, you know, protect us as a team."

The Mercedes call was a stark contrast to the Ferrari team, who at a key moment earlier in the race had dithered on asking Leclerc to move over to let Hamilton past, when the seven-time world champion was on a better strategy. Hamilton later argued it cost them a podium finish, at least. It suggested a team not all pulling in one direction -- and the tensions at F1's red team would explode into full public view one week later at Monza.

Antonelli's home Italian Grand Prix promised a moment of real jeopardy. Issues earlier in the season meant he needed a new engine and the back-of-the-grid penalty that came with it. Russell took a resounding pole position ahead of the two Ferrari drivers and it very much seemed game-on: yet another chance for Russell to try and change the momentum of the season, on Antonelli's home patch no less.

But Ferrari came into the race with bitterness lingering from Zandvoort. During qualifying at Monza, Hamilton -- the driver with the best mathematical shot at beating Antonelli -- had felt he was not given priority when it came to qualifying strategy. "The team was solely focused on trying to get an equal tow for each driver," Hamilton said, referring to the Monza trick of one driver giving his teammate an aerodynamic boost by doing a qualifying lap a certain distance ahead.

Hamilton continued: "We're at a point in the year where 59 points is a huge deficit to recover from, especially when Mercedes continue to be the leaders in speed. So yeah, we do have to work as a team. But have we been?" Hamilton then shrugged and shook his head, adding: "If and when that will ever change, we'll find out."

It seemed to be a clear plea from Hamilton for Ferrari to back him over Leclerc to try and wrestle the initiative back from Antonelli and Mercedes. Hamilton would get his answer in resounding fashion at Turn 1, when he got on the inside of Leclerc's car on the right-left first chicane. Leclerc refused to budge, pushing Hamilton wide and into the gravel. At the end of the second lap, Leclerc lost control of his car and crashed out. It was the most Ferrari of farces and appeared to end any chance the team had of making the rest of 2026 a two-team fight.

Antonelli's car, equipped with the new engine, was a rocketship. He was carving through the field, with each pass leading to a louder roar from the home crowd. He eventually caught Russell -- who had driven flawlessly out in front -- and, after one botched attempt at getting by which almost ended in the gravel -- Antonelli got ahead for a famous and emotional win, the first by an Italian at the Italian Grand Prix since 1966. Antonelli's 26 passes were the most recorded by a single driver at any race in F1 history. New engine or not, Antonelli had turned in the most magnificent of drives, dealt another bitter blow to Russell, and all while Ferrari fumbled a golden opportunity to give Mercedes some anxiety about a two-team fight. In a season of big moments, Monza was the moment.

As he stood on top of the podium, Antonelli soaked it all in. "The weekend itself was absolutely incredible," Antonelli said later. "Definitely so far the best day of my life, and an incredible memory. I couldn't wish for a better day." Two weeks later at Madrid's first-ever Spanish Grand Prix, Antonelli inched even closer to the title, as Norris' hopes of a win were undone by an awfully timed Safety Car. Antonelli would inherit the lead and keep Norris behind with a faultless drive under pressure to win Madring's processional debut event. Russell could only finish fifth.

Championship standings after Madrid:

Antonelli -- 292

Russell -- 211

Hamilton -- 191

Antonelli romps clear

Antonelli's perfect season appeared to hit a momentary roadblock in qualifying for Baku's Azerbaijan Grand Prix, where he dragged his front left tyre into the wall at Turn 1. It was a nightmare moment, a rare unforced error, as teammate Russell settled for second behind surprise polesitter Pierre Gasly. To anyone looking for a championship turnaround, there was historical precedent: Piastri's 2025 season had unraveled with unforced errors in Baku 12 months earlier. Was Antonelli about to trigger the same kind of implosion?

Out in front, Russell quickly got himself into the lead and controlled things from there, holding off old foe Verstappen over a tense final set of laps to record his first win since the Austrian Grand Prix. If Saturday had shown a glimpse of the raw side of the young Antonelli, Sunday showed why he was the champion-in-waiting, as he turned in a sensible and decisive drive to fifth, avoiding further drama on Baku's tight and twisty circuit. Russell's win felt important, but Antonelli had avoided a bigger points swing.

Verstappen's Baku performance had suggested a Red Bull resurgence and he confirmed it at the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia, a race which was as bizarre in name as it was in drama. A deluge before the start delayed the start, before F1's controversial new engines had a software glitch which caused a red flag before the end of the formation lap. When things finally restarted, Antonelli, Russell and Verstappen all traded places, before Verstappen took control of the race late on. As the finish neared, a final, decisive blow to Russell, as his Mercedes engine packed up a handful of laps from the end. Verstappen claimed Red Bull's first win of the year while Antonelli took an unanswered 18 points.

Russell's DNF was doubly costly, and it knocked him to the back of the grid in Singapore's Marina Bay street circuit. As had been the case a week earlier, Verstappen would control proceedings. Leclerc finished second, with Antonelli having a lonely race to third, but it saw him gain again -- Russell could only manage to fight back to ninth. The result meant Antonelli would go to Austin's United States Grand Prix with a slim mathematical chance of getting it done.

Championship standings after Singapore:

Antonelli -- 340

Russell -- 238

Hamilton -- 229

Antonelli gets it done in North America

If Monza a month earlier had been Antonelli's defining moment, Austin would feel like his unofficial coronation. He could claim the title if he won and Hamilton was fifth or lower and Russell was ninth or lower and arrived in Texas with a spring in his step. On Thursday, he seemed calm and relaxed and by Saturday he was in a perfect stride. Red Bull looked strong but Antonelli was on hand to deny them a pole position, delivering a beautiful lap late in Q3 to edge out Verstappen by 0.179 seconds. Hamilton and Russell settled for fifth and sixth on the grid, respectively, and suddenly the unlikely permutations felt a little less farfetched.

Race day came and it felt like Antonelli could get it done. But first he would have to navigate Verstappen -- the Red Bull opting to start on the grippier soft tyre off the line, while Antonelli and Mercedes opted for the medium, teasing a blockbuster run up COTA's hill to Turn 1. But anyone hoping for fireworks would be disappointed. Antonelli moved across to cover Verstappen at the start -- those sluggish getaways of the first part of the year a distant memory. The Italian immediately started building a lead as Verstappen was swallowed into a fight with the two Ferraris and Norris. Antonelli would only briefly surrender the lead in the pit stop phase of the race, but once back out in front he would disappear again, crossing the line 17 seconds clear of the next quickest car.

At one point, the maths made him champion, albeit briefly. Russell's race was hampered by a five-second time penalty, which turned an already poor event into a desperate one, and he soon dropped to ninth at the same point Hamilton was fifth -- exactly what Antonelli needed. By the finish, both had gained an additional place, meaning Hamilton finished fourth and Russell eighth.

Either way, it was a thumping win and felt like his championship affirmation moment. "Yes! That's how we f------ do it," Antonelli said on the radio after taking the chequered flag. "Let's do it."

Wolff felt like it was the standout drive of his young career. "For me, the best race that he's delivered so far," the Mercedes boss said. "Getting off the start with the inferior [medium] tyre and then controlling it at all times. The race of a champion who isn't the champion yet, but exceptional. So I think he's outperformed the car. Maybe it's a bit harsh to say, but I think his driving style just glues with the car."

It meant he needed just two points from the final five races to be champion and he would need to wait just seven days to start the party -- albeit after what he would describe as one of the most difficult weeks of his life.

Calm, jokey and mischievous in Austin, Antonelli arrived in Mexico City tense and unwell. He would miss Thursday's media session, later saying he felt "very bad." He added: "I had a high fever and stomach problems, so it hasn't been easy. But now I feel OK, just low on energy, just feel pretty tired, so it's going to be important to try and sleep well, because I haven't been sleeping well in these days, and hopefully tomorrow I will have more energy."

He clearly was not at 100% when qualifying came and, in a quirky twist on Austin, when his two competitors qualified down the order, they locked out the front row -- Hamilton claimed a spectacular first pole position for Ferrari, with Russell taking second place alongside his former teammate. Antonelli qualified fifth, which became fourth after a grid penalty for Verstappen. "I'm aware that definitely I haven't been driving well," Antonelli said afterwards. "I felt like already going to qualifying, I didn't feel great, and I felt a bit low on energy, so definitely, you know, it's not an excuse, but for sure, it hasn't been my finest performance."

The young Italian's plan to have a good night's sleep ahead of the biggest day of his life? "Bombard myself with melatonin," he said. Antonelli looked like a different man on Sunday, although he took a cautious approach to the start and standing restart that followed mid-race. There was drama ahead, with an clumsy Leclerc move on Hamilton handing Red Bull and Verstappen the win on a silver platter, but Antonelli didn't need to worry about any of it. A decisive move on Leclerc late on got him into the podium places and he spent the final laps of the race watching the two greatest drivers of his lifetime race for the win.

He admitted the view through his visor -- including that of Hamilton's Ferrari -- was getting blurrier as he neared the chequered flag. "[I was] already [crying] the lap before," Antonelli said later. "I think I lost probably two seconds because I was already crying, basically. I couldn't see clearly ahead. You know, I could see two Ferraris somehow with the tears."

Antonelli came home third, more than enough to clinch the title, to trigger wild celebrations with his team, and his family, who had flown in overnight from Italy to watch his crowning moment. "I am speechless, trying to process what just happened," Antonelli said later.

"A day I will remember forever. So grateful, thank you so much. I am going to enjoy every bit. I'm going to out with my family, friends and the team and we're just going to enjoy all the way because this is a very special moment and one we will remember forever."

The championship makes Antonelli F1's youngest, aged 20 years and 86 days.

Standings after Mexico City:

Antonelli -- 380

Verstappen -- 261

Hamilton -- 259

Russell -- 250

stories.headline: Messi to play in Argentina Jan. 19 for Inter Miami-River friendly
stories.summary: Lionel Messi will return to play at Estadio Monumental on Jan. 19 when Inter Miami travel to Buenos Aires to play River Plate.
stories.body:
Lionel Messi will return to play at Estadio Monumental on Jan. 19 for the first time since his Argentina farewell when Inter Miami travels to Buenos Aires to play River Plate in a friendly.

The eight-time Ballon d'Or winner has played a total of 29 matches for Argentina at El Monumental, the most recent on Oct. 6 in his national team farewell, where he played his 208th and final game for Argentina.

That match ended with his 126th goal capping a 21-year career for the legendary No. 10, which included two Copa América titles and a World Cup.

This game will mark the first time Messi has played a club match in his home country.

Over his career he has face Argentina clubs four times, including beating Estudiantes with Barcelona at the 2009 Club World Cup in United Arab Emirates and again when Barcelona defeated River for the 2015 Club World Cup in Japan.

Messi has also played two other friendlies vs. Argentina clubs: In 2018 with Barcelona beating Boca Juniors for the Joan Gamper trophy and a friendly in 2024 vs. his boyhood club, Newell's in Miami, which ended in a 1-1 draw.

River Plate is one of South America's most successful clubs, boasting 38 domestic titles and four Copa Libertadores trophies.

Earlier this week, Messi was named a finalist for the 2026 Major League Soccer MVP award. The Inter Miami captain seeks to become the first player to win the prize on three consecutive occasions.

Messi already clinched a record second straight Golden Boot award after scoring 26 goals in the 2026 regular season.

Miami said they expect Messi to be joined by Casemiro, Rodrigo De Paul, Luis Suárez, Nicolás Otamendi and Thiago Almada for the trip.

Inter Miami's previous preseason tours have included visits to Peru, Ecuador, Colombia and Puerto Rico.

Inter Miami will kick off the 2027 Major League Soccer season on Feb. 19 against FC Cincinnati at Nu Stadium.

stories.headline: AFL Draft: Key dates, FAQs, players to know, and more
stories.summary: The 2026 AFL draft is rapidly approaching, so here's your guide for what to know, including key dates and times, players to know, academy-linked names, and every club's pick.
stories.body:
The 2026 AFL Draft is fast approaching. Marvel Stadium will once more play host to the first round at 7:00pm AEDT on November 19, with the draft recommencing for the second round onwards on November 20.

Key dates and times
Where: Marvel Stadium

How to watch: Fox Footy

First round: Thursday, November 19, 7pm AEDT

Second round onwards: Friday, November 20, 7pm AEDT

Preseason and rookie draft: Monday, November 23, 3pm AEDT

Each club's picks

*As at Nov. 11
Adelaide: 15, 32, 35, 43, 54

Brisbane: 21, 27, 28, 45

Carlton: 13, 18, 31, 50, 59, 67, 73

Collingwood: 11, 30, 63, 64, 65

Essendon: 1, 17, 25, 69, 75, 78, 80 (plus second round compensation pick)

Fremantle: 19, 40, 58, 61, 68

Geelong: 36, 55, 60

Gold Coast: 8, 70, 72, 77

GWS: 9, 20, 26, 57

Hawthorn: 29, 37, 66, 74

Melbourne: 4, 14, 48, 51, 79

North Melbourne: 33, 49, 62

Port Adelaide: 7, 12, 22, 24, 34, 46

Richmond: 2, 5, 44, 76 (plus second round compensation pick)

St Kilda: 10, 16, 41

Sydney: 6, 38, 39, 47

West Coast: 3, 23, 56 (plus second round compensation pick)

Western Bulldogs: 42, 52, 53, 71

State of play and players to know
Essendon will be on the clock first, holding the top selection a decade on from the last time it took the number one pick to the AFL Draft. The Dons are expected to first bid on Port Adelaide-tied forward Dougie Cochrane, which will trigger a start-of-second-round compensation pick for the Bombers, Tigers and Eagles.

There are familial lines drawn throughout an exciting 2008-born cohort. Cody Walker is the son of high-flying Blue Andrew and will be headed to Princes Park. Cochrane is the son of former North Melbourne and Port Adelaide midfielder Stuart, though he isn't eligible to either team under the 100-game father-son rule. Instead, he's eligible to join the Power as part of their Next Generation Academy as an Indigenous prospect.

Top-10 riser Sam Gayfer is the nephew of 1990 premiership Pie Mick, and Koby LeCras brings goalkicking pedigree via 2018 premiership uncle Mark.

There will be up to five club-tied talents picked in the first round of the AFL Draft. But that won't necessarily result in an extended first night. Over the past five years the first round has averaged out to 25 selections accounting for father-son and academy bids, but clubs are expecting a number closer to the traditional 18 picks in the final intake of the 18-team competition.

Stricter stipulations around matching bids is at play, with clubs only able to use a maximum of two selections when matching for a club-tied prospect, meaning the selections of Port Adelaide, Carlton, Brisbane and GWS will be absorbed as early bids are matched.

We could see a record number of Indigenous talents picked in the first round. The high-water mark was four in 2005 and 2014, and all of Cochrane, Walker, Caylen Murray (Lions Academy), Toby Krasna and Jake Eime could be taken in the first round in 2026.

Thirteen of the top prospects have already been invited to Marvel Stadium on November 19.

Ethan Drever, Arki Butler and Heath Mellody are all still in contention to be the open pool No. 1 pick, with Harry Van Hattum, Gus Teixeira, Mitch Harris and Ethan Matthews (Giants Academy) rounding out the group on top of draft boards alongside Cochrane and Walker.

Murray, Gayfer, Wil Malady and Leo Steed have also received invites in a sign of club interest on night one.

Around 65 picks are expected to be taken across both nights which would surpass the 60 selections last year.

stories.headline: First-half romp powers Jillaroos' fourth-straight Rugby League World Cup salute
stories.summary: Australia's Jillaroos have blown away New Zealand 34-10 to win a fourth-straight Women's Rugby League World Cup.
stories.body:
Australia have underlined their women's rugby league dominance with a 34-10 annihilation of New Zealand in the World Cup final.

The Jillaroos did the damage with six first-half tries on Sunday at Suncorp Stadium, with winger Jaime Chapman recording a brilliant hat-trick before the break to cap a historic tournament.

It was Australia's fourth straight Cup triumph, following a 54-4 win in the final four years ago and coming after New Zealand won the first three tournaments between 2000-08.

Chapman carried two players more than 10 metres to score her first, before flying into the corner for another and then busting through four tacklers for a sensational 70-metre solo effort.

Her treble gave her the equal record for tries in a World Cup -- for men or women -- at 13, matching the Kiwi Ferns' Honey Hireme-Smiler from 2017.

It seemed inevitable that she would go clear in the second half.

But both teams struggled in the Brisbane humidity, with the Kiwi Ferns' try in the finals seconds the only points of an error-riddled second period.

For the Jillaroos there were several poignant narratives to come out of the win.

Coach Jess Skinner's controversial decision to play five-eighth Jesse Southwell and drop Jocelyn Kelleher paid dividends.

Southwell schemed with the ball, landed five goals and was the perfect foil for half Tarryn Aiken, who controlled play with confidence and skill.

Chapman played in the pool games and semi-final in the 2022 World Cup but has now put an indelible stamp on a final.

"There is no better win than winning the World Cup on home turf," she told Channel Seven.

"We connected the first day we came into camp."

Fullback Tamika Upton sat out the tournament four years ago with a calf injury but now the five-time premiership winner has every team accolade in the game to her credit.

Prop Millie Elliott retires with a fairytale ending while dual international Sariah Paki, who was chased by the Ferns to play for them, has now won the World Cup in two sports after triumphing with the Australian rugby sevens side in 2022.

All the talk before the clash was the danger posed by New Zealand's Golden Boot winner and strike centre Stacey Waaka.

The former rugby union star, who had scored nine tries in the tournament, was snuffed out by Jillaroos captain Isabelle Kelly, who confronted Waaka all match and gave her no space.

As the Jillaroos' big guns stood up, centre Jessica Sergis scored her 23rd try in 18 Tests with a 70m dash through the middle off an undetected forward pass.

Aiken turned second-rower Shaylee Bent inside for the second try of the match while Upton started and finished a movement that had her attacking fingerprints all over it.

Ferns fullback Apii Nicholls was her side's best player in a dynamic display until she tore a hamstring in the 66th minute.
